steps: Flake the tuna with its oil, or fry the bacon until just cooked.
Mix in the rest of the filling ingredients.
Roll out the pastry, spread with the filling and roll up lengthways.
Wrap in clingwrap and freeze for about 30 minutes.
Slice 10 mm thick, place on a greased tray and bake at 180°C for about 10 minutes until golden.
Fry the onion in the butter until soft.
Add the livers, stock and seasonings and fry until cooked.
Stir in the sour cream last, take off the heat and serve on toast.

data.title: Chicken Livers in Tomato Sauce
data.headnote: Lovely as a starter or light supper.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Blend the sauce ingredients well, then cook down in a pot until thick.
Heat the oil and butter and fry the livers for about 5 minutes.
Put the livers in a dish, pour over the sauce and serve with fresh rolls or Melba toast.

data.title: Renette's Layered Fish Starter
data.headnote: "Baie lekker!" Layered in the fridge and mixed just before serving.

steps: Layer the fish, onion, potato, gherkin, cheese, salad sprinkle and egg in a dish, finishing with mayonnaise on top.
Sprinkle with peri-peri and refrigerate.
Mix just before serving with Melba toast.

checks: Quantities for cheese, eggs and mayo aren't given, and the original doesn't say whether the haddock is cooked (smoked haddock is usually poached first).

data.title: Renette's Bacon & Cheese Toasts

steps: Fry the onion and bacon. Mix with the cheese, egg, mayo and seasoning (more cheese if it's runny, more mayo if it's stiff).
Spread on bread, cut each slice in 3 and grill until golden. Watch closely, it burns easily.

tips: The mixture keeps in the fridge for up to a week.

groups.heading: Sauce
ingredients: 8 to 10 small tomatoes, peeled and roughly chopped

groups.heading: Toasties
ingredients: Mozzarella balls, each cut in three
Milk seasoned with salt and coarse pepper

groups.heading: Method
steps: For the sauce, fry the onion, garlic and oregano in olive oil, add the tomatoes and wine and cook until soft. Add basil just before serving.
Dip one side of each bread round in the seasoned milk.
Sandwich a slice of mozzarella and basil between two rounds, wet sides in, and press the edges together like a jaffle.
Dip in egg and fry until golden. Serve with the tomato sauce.
Cook everything together, thinning with milk to the consistency you like.
Cook everything together until thick and creamy.
Serve with fried croutons.

data.title: Zannie's Mussel Soup

ingredients: 1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (or 1 tsp dried)
2 chicken stock cubes in 750 ml boiling water
steps: Soften the onion, garlic and parsley in butter. Stir in the flour.
Pour in the hot stock, then stir in everything else.
Cook about 15 minutes over low heat. Add cream if you like.

tips: For extra flavour, make up 1 packet Royco Seafood soup and halve the stock and flour.

ingredients: 1 packet minestrone (or mutton and vegetable) soup powder
Salt, pepper and 2 ml curry powder
steps: Boil the bones in the water for 1 hour.
Add the carrot, onion, potato and celery and cook until soft.
Mix the soup powder with a little cold water and add, with the macaroni and bay leaves. Boil 30 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper and curry.
Add the tomato purée and oats and cook 10 to 20 minutes more. Add the parsley just before serving.

data.title: Red Lentil Soup
data.headnote: "Delish!"

ingredients: 2 to 3 vegetable or beef stock cubes
steps: Boil the water, stock, lentils and tomatoes for 20 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Add the seasoning, sugar and cordial and blend smooth.

groups.heading: Meat
ingredients: 3 tomatoes, peeled and chopped (or 1 x 410 g tin)

groups.heading: Method
steps: Fry the onion and garlic in the oil. Add the tomato and mince and fry further.
Add the rest of the meat ingredients and simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Cook the noodles according to the packet.
White sauce in the microwave: melt the butter in a large jug, stir in the flour and seasoning, add the milk gradually and cook on high, stirring every minute, until thick.
Layer noodles, meat, sauce and cheese, ending with cheese. Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes.
Fry the peppers, bacon and mushrooms.
Cook the soup powder in the stock with the oregano.
Mix everything with the chicken and noodles and spoon into a greased dish.
Pour over the cream, top with the cheese and bake 45 minutes at 180°C.

data.title: Chicken, Rice & Blatjang Chip Bake

ingredients: 1 chicken, cooked without salt, deboned and chopped
1 packet cream of chicken soup, made with 2 litres water and cooked
steps: Mix everything together and spoon into an ovenproof dish.
Top with cheese and paprika and bake at 180°C for 20 minutes until heated through.

tips: Freezes well unbaked. Swap the chips for Bacon Kips if you like.

steps: Brown the chops lightly. Add the onion, curry, turmeric and cumin and fry 3 minutes more.
Add the flour and chutney.
Heat the stock and lemon juice and add. Simmer slowly 2 hours or until tender.
Add the pineapple and apple 20 minutes before serving.

ingredients: Pinch of nutmeg, salt and black pepper
steps: Gently fry the onion and garlic in the butter. Stir in the flour.
Add the cream and milk and cook over low heat about 3 minutes, stirring, until it starts to thicken (not too thick).
Stir in the mustard and feta, then gently fold in the fish and the chives.
Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper and serve over pasta.

data.title: Sweet-and-Sour Curried Peach Salad

steps: Soften the onions in the oil. Add the curry, turmeric and sauce powder and fry 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the fruit and cook a few minutes, stirring so it doesn't catch.

tips: Add sliced pickled cucumber, 125 g seedless raisins or a chopped green pepper if you like.

ingredients: 1 kg raw broccoli, in small florets

groups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the salad ingredients. Mix the dressing and pour over.
Leave for 24 hours or longer before serving.
Put the lettuce in the bottom of a deep salad bowl and layer the rest on top.
Cover completely with the mayonnaise, cover and refrigerate for 24 hours.
Mix well just before serving.
Fry the onions in oil until translucent.
Add the dry ingredients and fry about 3 minutes (careful, it catches).
Add the rest and cook through.
Cool, pour over sosaties or chops and marinate for at least 24 hours.

ingredients: 2 tbsp (25 ml) melted butter or oil
steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar, then add the butter and half the milk.
Sift the dry ingredients and mix in, then add the rest of the milk gradually to a smooth batter.
Don't stir again once mixed. Cook spoonfuls on a hot plate or pan.
Whisk the eggs and brandy well. Add everything else and whisk smooth.
Let it stand a little, then cook thin pancakes. Sprinkle with cinnamon sugar while hot.

data.title: Pancakes (Kook en Geniet)

steps: Whisk the eggs and milk. Sift in the dry ingredients bit by bit, mixing well each time until smooth.
Let it stand a while (the pancakes will be lighter); it can stay in the fridge overnight.

data.source: Marikie's Christmas Recipe Folder 2009 (from Kook en Geniet)

ingredients: ¼ cup salt (or a little less)
2½ packets (10 g each) instant yeast (1 packet per kg flour)
steps: Rub the butter into the dry ingredients. (You can freeze this mix in 1 kg bags at this point.)
Add the yeast, the lukewarm liquid and vinegar and knead well (melted butter on your hands helps). Leave to double.
Knock back, shape into balls, let rise again and fry in hot oil.
Sift the dry ingredients. Whisk the egg, oil, milk and water.
Mix together, spoon into a muffin tin and bake 10 minutes at 200°C.
Sift the dry ingredients. Whisk the cream, water and eggs.
Mix, drop spoonfuls onto a greased tray and bake 10 to 15 minutes at 200°C until golden.

ingredients: 1 cup grated red viennas and/or 250 g bacon bits, fried
steps: Mix the cheese, eggs, onion and meat. Add the rest and mix well.
Spoon into muffin tins and bake at 180°C for about 30 minutes.
Spread chutney over the hot muffins and serve straight away.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the crushed chips with melted margarine and press into a tart dish, keeping a little for the top.
Fry the bacon and onion.
Make a white sauce with the margarine, flour and milk, then beat in the eggs.
Add the bacon, onion, cheese, asparagus and mushrooms, mix and pour into the crust.
Bake at 180°C for 1 hour. Decorate with parsley and the reserved crumbs.

data.title: Success Cake (Hot-Milk Sponge)

steps: Beat the eggs and sugar. Sift the flour, baking powder and salt.
Bring the milk and oil to the boil together.
Mix the flour into the egg mixture, then add the vanilla and the boiling milk mixture.
Bake at 180°C for 25 to 30 minutes (cupcakes 15 to 20 minutes).

tips: For chocolate cake use 2 cups flour and ¾ cup cocoa.

ingredients: Icing sugar and a little lemon juice, to sandwich
steps: Sift the dry ingredients. Cream the butter and sugar, then beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Combine and pipe biscuits with a cookie press or piping bag.
Bake about 10 minutes at 180°C.
Sandwich with icing sugar mixed with a little lemon juice.
Sift the dry ingredients and add the sugar.
Add the milk gradually, mixing well, then the beaten yolks and the butter.
Whisk the whites stiff and fold in. Cook in a hot waffle iron.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Sift the dry ingredients. Coarsely grate in the butter and rub in.
Beat the eggs and milk and add to make a stiff dough.
Roll out thinly, spread with jam and roll up like a Swiss roll. Cut into 3 cm wheels.
Arrange in a deep greased ovenproof dish and pour over the mixed sauce.
Bake at 180°C for 40 to 45 minutes until golden.
Melt the sugar, water, butter, syrup and salt and cook until the sugar dissolves. Take off the heat and add the condensed milk.
Cook about 25 minutes, stirring constantly (it catches easily), until slightly grainy.
Off the heat, stir in the vanilla and pour into a greased tin.

resolvedChecks.note: The water quantity is partly illegible in the original ("! kop"); ½ cup is the usual amount.
resolvedChecks.resolution: ½ cup water kept (the usual amount).

steps: Melt the margarine and marshmallows in the microwave for 1½ to 2 minutes.
Mix in the Rice Krispies, press into a greased tin and cut into squares while still slightly warm.
Cream the margarine and sugar and beat in the eggs, then the peanut butter.
Dissolve the bicarb in the milk, add the vanilla and stir in.
Mix in the rest of the ingredients.
Roll into walnut-sized balls, flatten with a fork and bake 10 to 15 minutes at 180°C.

data.title: Meringue Roulade with Lemon Cream

groups.heading: Meringue
steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Spray a Swiss roll tin, line with baking paper and spray the paper.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks, add the castor sugar bit by bit, then the brown sugar, and whisk until stiff (don't overbeat).
Spread evenly in the tin and sprinkle with almonds. Bake about 12 minutes.
Lower to 170°C and bake 25 minutes more, covering loosely with paper if the nuts brown.
Rest 5 minutes, turn out onto baking paper, peel off the lining and cool 15 minutes. Trim the edges.

groups.heading: To finish
ingredients: Extra toasted almonds or other nuts
Fresh fruit (banana, berries) or preserved ginger (optional)

groups.heading: Lemon cream
steps: Heat the butter and sugar in a double boiler. Add the beaten yolks and lemon juice, whisking constantly, until thick. Cool.
Whip the cream stiff and fold in the lemon mixture.

groups.heading: Assemble
steps: Spread the cream over the meringue, top with fruit or nuts and roll up from one side (Marikie prefers the short side).
Chill a few hours. Dust with toasted nuts and icing sugar.

tips: It freezes well; thaw slowly for about 45 minutes.
checks: The almond weight is printed as "?0 gram" in the original; 70 g is a best reading.

ingredients: 5 ml bicarbonate of soda, dissolved in a little warm water
steps: Sift the flour, baking powder, cream of tartar and salt. Grate in the butter and rub in well.
Whisk the buttermilk, cream, eggs and sugar well, then add the bicarb.
Combine. Shape 12 balls for each of 3 loaf tins and bake about 1 hour at 180°C.
Break each ball in two with a fork and dry out at about 70°C.

data.title: Yoghurt Loaf
data.headnote: "Quick, easy and delicious!"

steps: Mix everything and pour into a small greased loaf tin.
Bake 1 hour at 180°C.
Stir everything together and pour into a loaf tin. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake at 180°C for 45 to 60 minutes.

data.title: Banana Bread

steps: Melt the milk and butter together.
Mix the flour and sugar and add the milk mixture.
Whisk the eggs and salt, add the bananas and mix everything together.
Dissolve the bicarb in the extra milk and stir in evenly.
Pour into a greased loaf tin. Bake 25 minutes at 190°C, then 25 minutes at 170°C.

data.source: Marikie's Christmas Recipe Folder 2009; screenshot of the same recipe

data.title: Microwave Mealie Bread

steps: Mix everything and pour into a round microwave ring pan.
Microwave on high for 12 minutes.

checks: The milk and sugar quantities are illegible in the original.

data.title: Deep-Dish Apple Pie with Salted Butterscotch
data.headnote: Buttery rye pastry, tender apples and a rich salted butterscotch sauce.

groups.heading: Pastry
steps: Pulse the flours, icing sugar and salt in a processor. Add the butter and pulse to rough crumbs, then the water until it comes together.
Press together, wrap and chill 1 hour.

groups.heading: Filling
ingredients: 7 to 8 Pink Lady apples, peeled, cored and cut into ½ cm wedges

groups.heading: Pie
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C with a rack on the lowest rung.
Roll each half of the dough 3 mm thick and line a deep square dish with one. Chill 10 minutes.
Whisk the sugar, cornflour, spices, brandy and cream, then toss through the apples.
Fill the case, dot with butter and cover with the second sheet (or a lattice). Seal, brush with egg and sprinkle with sugar. Cut steam slits.
Bake 15 minutes low, then 60 to 65 minutes at 180°C on the middle rung, covering with foil for the last 15 to 20 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes on a rack.

groups.heading: Butterscotch
steps: Melt the butter, add the sugar and cook to a deep caramel, 5 to 6 minutes.
Add the cream and simmer until thick, 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in the vanilla and salt. Serve with the pie and vanilla ice cream.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C and grease a 12-cup brownie tray well.
Mix the base ingredients with a spatula to a soft dough. Press 30 g into each cup and bake 25 minutes. Lower the oven to 160°C.
Mix the curd ingredients, divide among the cups and bake 20 minutes. Cool, then chill at least 2 hours.
Boil the sugar and water. At 110°C start whipping the whites on medium; at 118°C pour the syrup in a thin stream.
Whip on high until the bowl is cool, about 10 minutes. Add the salt and vanilla and beat 30 seconds.
Pipe onto the squares and toast with a blowtorch.

data.title: Malva Pudding Milk Tart
data.headnote: Two South African classics in one dish: malva pudding topped with a layer of milk tart.

groups.heading: Milk tart layer
steps: Bring the milk and cinnamon to the boil and set aside.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, cornflour, flour and vanilla until smooth, then whisk in the hot milk.
Cook in a pot over medium heat with the butter until thick.
Spread over the pudding, dust with cinnamon and chill at least 2 hours. Cut into squares.

groups.heading: Pudding
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C and spray a 32 cm rectangular dish.
Beat the eggs and sugar until pale, then add the butter, milk and jam. Sift in the flour and mix.
Mix the vinegar into the bicarb (it fizzes) and add quickly. Pour into the dish and bake 50 minutes.
Melt the syrup ingredients together. Loosen the hot pudding's edges, prick with a fork and ladle the syrup over. Cool completely.

data.title: Old-Fashioned Fudge

steps: Grease a 12-cup brownie tray well.
Melt the butter, add the sugar and stir. Add the cream and condensed milk and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Boil to 115°C (soft ball: a drop in cold water rolls into a ball).
Beat with a hand mixer 3 to 4 minutes until thick and dull.
Divide among the cups and set at room temperature for 90 minutes. Turn out with a good thump.

data.credit: Keshree Chundriah for Le Creuset South Africa

data.title: Beef Bourguignon
data.headnote: The French classic with a splash of brandy, perfect for a cold evening.

ingredients: 2 kg beef, in large bite-sized pieces
1 cup flour (for dusting and beurre manié)
1 tbsp roast rub (or a bouquet garni)
2 tbsp beef stock in 500 ml hot water
steps: Fry the bacon in 3 tbsp oil until lightly browned and lift out.
Sear the beef in batches. Return the bacon and meat and deglaze with the wine (and brandy).
Add the garlic, tomato paste, stock, carrots, celery, spices and 2 tsp pepper. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently 2 hours.
30 minutes before the end, caramelise the shallots slowly in 30 g butter (10 to 15 minutes). Fry the mushrooms in the remaining butter.
Mix about 1 tbsp soft butter and 1 tbsp flour to a paste (beurre manié) and stir in bit by bit to thicken. Add the shallots and mushrooms and simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
Season and scatter with parsley. Serve with mash or baguette.

resolvedChecks.note: The original never says when the celery goes in or gives the beurre manié quantities; small amounts (about 1 tbsp each) are typical.
resolvedChecks.resolution: Celery already goes in with the carrots; beurre manié set at about 1 tbsp each.

ingredients: 1.5 kg mussels in shells, scrubbed and debearded
steps: Rinse the mussels and discard any open ones that won't close when squeezed.
Soften the onion and garlic in the butter. Add the thyme, bay and wine and turn the heat to high.
Add the mussels, cover and steam 6 to 10 minutes until open. Discard the herbs and any closed mussels.
Stir in the cream and parsley, season and serve with lots of bread.

data.title: Sparkling Wine & Garlic Mussel Pot

ingredients: 500 ml Méthode Cap Classique or sparkling wine
steps: Soften the onion in the oil. Add the garlic, lemon peel and thyme for 2 minutes.
Turn up the heat, add the mussels and bubbly, cover and cook 5 to 8 minutes until open.
Simmer, season and reduce slightly. Serve with dill and bread.

tips: Stir in half a cup of cream once the mussels are cooked for a richer sauce.

ingredients: 2 red onions or leeks, thinly sliced
steps: Brush each phyllo sheet with oil and stack in four sets of three. Cover with a damp cloth.
Blanch the spinach, refresh in iced water and squeeze very dry in a cloth.
Caramelise the onion lightly (in the butter), add the garlic for 2 minutes, then the spinach off the heat. Crumble in the feta and season carefully.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (fan) and grease a 30 cm shallow casserole.
Layer phyllo and a third of the filling three times, finishing with phyllo. Brush with oil, crinkle the edges in and sprinkle with sesame.
Bake 50 minutes until golden. Serve warm with a Greek salad.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Squeeze the sausage meat out of the casings and mix with the garlic, ginger, chilli, soy, honey and spring onion.
Roll into about 30 meatballs with wet hands.
Fry in two batches for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and cooked.
Pour in the teriyaki, toss and reduce about 5 minutes until sticky. Serve with the extras.

data.title: Asian Coconut Chicken Broth
data.headnote: Very little effort for a lot of flavour, and even better the next day.

groups.heading: To serve
ingredients: Baby purple kale, toasted sesame seeds, grilled lime and sliced chilli

groups.heading: Method
steps: Blitz the fennel, ginger, garlic, chilli and onion to a paste. Cook in the coconut oil over medium-low heat 5 to 10 minutes.
Add the chicken, lime leaves, star anise, peppercorns and water to just cover. Simmer covered 45 minutes, turn and poach 30 to 45 minutes more.
Lift out the chicken. Add the coconut milk and soy and simmer 30 minutes. Season with fish sauce and strain.
Shred the chicken and return it to the broth.
Blanch the coriander 5 seconds, refresh and dry, then blend with the zest, garlic and oil. Add lime juice and season.
Serve the broth boiling hot with kale, coriander oil, sesame, chilli and grilled lime.

groups.heading: Filling
ingredients: 30 g basil, chopped (plus sprigs to garnish)

groups.heading: Method
steps: Blend the butter until soft, add the flour to crumbs, then the egg until it comes together. Rest 20 minutes in the fridge.
Press into 4 mini flan dishes and blind-bake at 200°C for 15 minutes (chill first so it doesn't shrink).
Beat the eggs, milk and basil and season.
Fry the tomatoes in the oil until they pop. Divide among the cases and pour over the egg mixture.
Bake at 180°C for 10 to 15 minutes until set and golden. Garnish with basil.

data.title: Green Broth with Bacon & Lasagne Sheets
data.headnote: A bright green broth packed with autumn vegetables.

ingredients: 500 g Kassler chops or bacon, cubed
2 to 3 litres vegetable stock or bone broth
Extra virgin olive oil and lemon
steps: Fry the Kassler or bacon in the oil until crisp and set aside.
Soften the garlic, leeks and celery gently 5 minutes without colouring. Add the kale and chard for a minute.
Add the stock, bring to a simmer, then take off the heat and blend smooth (strain if you like).
Simmer gently 20 minutes, seasoning and adding stock as needed.
10 minutes before serving add the lemon rind and lasagne sheets; 2 minutes before, add the spinach, asparagus, broccoli and peas.
Serve topped with the crisp bacon, olive oil and a squeeze of lemon.

data.title: Caramelised Cauliflower Soup with Lemon Burnt Butter

groups.heading: Method
steps: Sweat the leeks and garlic in the oil 5 minutes. Add the cauliflower for 5 minutes, then stock to just cover. Simmer 40 minutes.
Cool, blend with the cream and reheat. Season.
Roast the oiled, seasoned florets at 200°C for 25 minutes, then add the Parmesan and roast 5 to 10 minutes more.
Brown the butter to a rich gold, take off the heat and add the lemon juice.
Serve the soup drizzled with burnt butter, topped with florets and greens.
Sauté the onion, chorizo and garlic in the oil 5 minutes. Add the carrots for 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in the chopped rosemary, tomatoes and stock. Boil, then simmer 30 minutes.
Add the prawns and saffron and simmer gently 5 minutes.
Scatter with rosemary and Parmesan and serve with bread.

data.title: French Onion Soup
data.headnote: Caramelised onions and beef stock under buttery croûtes and molten Gruyère.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Melt the butter over low heat, add the onions and sugar and cook, stirring regularly, until sticky and caramelised (at least 30 minutes).
Add the vinegar and let it evaporate. Off the heat, stir in the flour, then the stock, pepper and bay.
Stir over the heat until slightly thickened, then cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Brush the bread with butter on both sides and toast in a 200°C oven or under the grill.
Divide the soup among ovenproof bowls, top each with 3 croûtes and the Gruyère and grill until bubbling. Finish with parsley.

data.source: Le Creuset SA recipe (saved PDF); second French Onion Soup PDF in Recipes folder

data.title: Roasted Tomato Soup

ingredients: Coconut cream and fresh basil, to serve
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Put all the vegetables in a dish, drizzle with oil and season generously.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes until soft. Cool slightly and blend smooth (squeeze the garlic out of its skins).
Heat in a pot with the stock for 10 minutes.
Serve with coconut cream, basil and toasted ciabatta.

data.credit: Health Alignment for Le Creuset South Africa

data.title: Spicy Chorizo & Tomato Broth with Cannellini Beans
data.headnote: Spanish-style, served with shard-like puff pastry dippers.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Sweat the celery, onion and garlic in the oil 5 minutes. Add the vine tomatoes, chorizo and paprika and fry 3 to 5 minutes.
Remove half the tomatoes and chorizo and set aside. Add the tinned tomatoes, chilli and 1.5 litres stock and simmer 25 minutes. Season.
Cut the pastry into uneven shards, brush with egg, sprinkle with seeds and salt and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes.
Toss the beans with the reserved chorizo and tomatoes, divide among bowls and ladle over the broth. Serve with basil and the dippers.

groups.heading: Toppings
ingredients: Sour cream, tortilla chips, sliced tomatoes, diced red onion, chilli, coriander and pink pickled onions

groups.heading: Method
steps: Fry the garlic, onion, chipotle and spices until soft.
Add the tomatoes and paste, simmer 5 minutes, then add stock to the consistency you like. Simmer 20 to 30 minutes and season.
Remove the chipotles, add the vinegar and blend if you want it smooth.
Serve hot in mugs with all the toppings.

ingredients: 125 g whole Camembert, at room temperature
steps: Mix the yeast, water and sugar and leave a few minutes.
Make a well in the flour, add the yeast mix and gradually stir in. Knead 10 minutes until springy. Cover and leave to double, about 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Arrange even balls in a ring in a greased 26 cm skillet, leaving space in the middle.
Brush with egg, sprinkle with salt and sesame and bake 30 to 35 minutes until hollow-sounding.
Nestle the scored Camembert in the centre, drizzle with honey and bake 5 to 10 minutes until oozing.

data.title: The New Prawn Cocktail
data.headnote: Coconut-crumbed prawns on a melon and cucumber salad. No soggy salad boats.

groups.heading: Prawns
ingredients: 12 tiger prawns, peeled and deveined, tails on

groups.heading: Salad
ingredients: 6 baby cucumbers (4 sliced, 2 shaved into ribbons)
Black sesame seeds and micro herbs

groups.heading: Method
steps: Dust the prawns in seasoned flour and paprika, dip in egg and coat in the coconut-panko mix.
Shallow-fry 1 to 2 minutes a side until golden.
Divide the melon and cucumber among 6 small dishes, squeeze over lime and top with 3 prawns each.
Drizzle with Japanese mayo and garnish with sesame and micro herbs.

data.title: MasterChef Chilli Con Carne
data.headnote: Deep, dark and smoky with chipotle, cocoa and treacle. If you can, leave it overnight and reheat.

ingredients: 1 kg beef mince (or lean chuck, cubed)
1 bunch coriander, leaves picked and stalks chopped
2 tsp chilli powder, or to taste
steps: Brown the meat in batches in the oil over high heat. Set aside.
Stir-fry the onions briefly until lightly browned. Turn down the heat, add the garlic, green chillies and coriander stalks and cook until soft. Return the meat.
Add the tomato purée and cook a couple of minutes.
Seed the chipotles and grind with rock salt. Stir in with all the other spices and heat to release the oils.
Add the wine, cocoa and treacle and reduce until the wine is absorbed.
Add the red pepper, tomatoes, stock and kidney beans and simmer 2 hours, stirring often.
Season, scatter with coriander leaves and serve with sour cream.

resolvedChecks.note: The kidney beans are listed but never added in the original. Adding them with the stock is standard.
resolvedChecks.resolution: Kidney beans go in with the stock.

data.title: Vanilla Pound Cake
data.headnote: Equal weights of butter, sugar, eggs and flour. It scales easily for bigger tins (see tip).

steps: Cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add the eggs one by one, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour; don't overmix.
Line a 20 cm tin with baking paper and bake at 170°C for about 1 hour 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cover with foil if the top browns too fast.
Rest 10 minutes in the tin, then cool on a rack.

tips: For a 28 cm tin use 625 g each butter, sugar and flour, 12 eggs and 12.5 ml vanilla. For 35 cm, make that batch twice.

data.title: Chocolate Cake with Chocolate Butter Icing
data.headnote: A one-bowl oil-and-yoghurt chocolate cake.

groups.heading: Cake
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line two 22 cm tins.
Combine everything except the bicarb and hot water. Dissolve the bicarb in the water, add and beat well.
Divide between the tins and bake 35 to 45 minutes, turning halfway, until a tester comes out clean.
Rest 10 minutes in the tins, then cool on a rack.

groups.heading: Icing
steps: Sift the icing sugar and cocoa over the butter and beat in the eggs one at a time until it's the right consistency.

tips: The icing uses raw eggs, so use very fresh eggs and skip it for anyone pregnant, elderly or very young.

resolvedChecks.note: The icing uses raw eggs.
resolvedChecks.resolution: Raw-egg note moved to a tip.

steps: Slowly whisk the icing sugar into the egg white until a thick, stiff paste forms.
Colour as you like and keep in small piping bags until needed.

data.title: Italian Meringue
data.headnote: A stable cooked meringue for topping and piping. You need a sugar thermometer.

steps: Bring the sugar and water to the boil, stirring until dissolved. Brush down the sides with a wet pastry brush.
Cook to 115°C (soft ball). Start whisking the whites and cream of tartar to soft peaks.
When the syrup reaches 121°C, pour it gradually into the whites with the mixer on high.
Beat on medium until cooled to room temperature, thick and glossy.

data.title: Stuffed Courgette Flowers with Baby Marrow Velouté
data.headnote: Courgette flowers filled with porcini and goat's cheese, with a herb crumble, baby marrow velouté and a garden flower salad.

groups.heading: Herb crumble
steps: Rub everything together to a rough crumble and bake at 175°C for 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes.

groups.heading: Flower salad
ingredients: Edible flowers (rocket, borage, pansy, marigold, bean, rosemary, fennel)

groups.heading: Brioche

Mix in the wakame. Put in a greased loaf tin, cover with a damp cloth and rise somewhere warm until doubled (at least an hour).

data.title: Stuffed Saddle of Lamb with Sweet Potato Dauphinoise
data.headnote: Rolled saddle of lamb with an apricot and pistachio stuffing, served with sautéed cauliflower, braised red onions, sweet potato dauphinoise and a minted demi-glace.

groups.heading: Lamb
ingredients: Olive oil, sea salt and pepper
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C. Trim the saddle so it rolls into a neat log.
Toast the cumin, then grind with ¼ tsp each salt and pepper and the sumac. Rub half over the lamb.
Chop the apricots and pine nuts and mix with the breadcrumbs, pistachios, oil and the rest of the spice mix.
Open the lamb out, season, lay over the Parma ham and pile the stuffing along the centre. Fold over and tie every 2 to 3 cm.
Sear 3 to 4 minutes a side in an ovenproof pan, then roast seam-side down for 35 minutes, turning and basting halfway. Rest 10 to 15 minutes.

groups.heading: Stuffing
ingredients: 150 g dried apricots, soaked overnight and drained

groups.heading: Dauphinoise (start first)
steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C. Slice the sweet potato 3 mm thick. Grate in the garlic (skins stay behind), season and mix with the cream.
Press into a gratin dish; the cream should come just below the top layer. Bake 1 to 1½ hours until tender. Turn down the oven if the cream splits.

groups.heading: Sides
steps: Cauliflower: sauté the garlic in 2 tbsp oil and the butter, add the florets and cook about 12 minutes. Fry the cumin, crumbs and pine nuts in 1 tbsp oil until golden, toss through with the parsley.
Onions: brown in the butter, add the stock, vinegar, sugar and salt, cover with baking paper and simmer until soft. Add the thyme.
Demi-glace: toast the cumin, add the demi-glace and bring to the boil. Add the tomato and mint and whisk in the butter.
Slice the lamb thickly and serve with everything.

data.title: La Mouette Salt & Pepper Prawns with Chorizo Popcorn

groups.heading: Sweet corn purée
ingredients: Pinch each of salt and sugar

groups.heading: Elements
steps: Purée: sweat the onion in oil, add the corn for 2 minutes, then the sugar, salt and vinegar. Add the cream and water, cook 5 minutes, blend, sieve and chill in a squeeze bottle.
Dressing: reduce the fish sauce, sugar, water and tamarind until syrupy. Cool and add the olive oil.
Popcorn: pop in hot oil with the lid on, then season with salt, sugar and smoked paprika.
Baby corn: blanch, refresh, halve, oil, season and char in a griddle pan.

groups.heading: Finish
steps: Dredge the prawns in milk, then the salt and pepper flour. Deep-fry at 190°C until golden.
Dot the plate with purée and add chorizo, spring onion, corn, popcorn and baby corn. Top with prawns, radish and micro greens and drizzle with dressing.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Guacamole: blitz everything except the cream until smooth, then add the cream briefly (don't overmix).
Papaya: peel and julienne. Boil the vinegar, water, sugar, cinnamon and habanero, pour over and steep 45 minutes.
Oil: warm the oil with the citrus and chilli to 50°C and steep 5 minutes.
Tuna: slice and season with salt, pepper and the infused oil.
Foam: blend everything with a stick blender, keep aerating until foamy.
Crisps: knead the masa and water, rest 30 minutes, press thin, cut into petals, dry-fry both sides, then deep-fry at 180°C.
Mango: blend to a smooth purée.
Plate the tuna with dots of guacamole and mango, papaya, crisps and foam.

data.title: Black Macarons
data.headnote: Italian-meringue macarons tinted black.

steps: Sift the icing sugar and almonds separately, then combine.
Start whisking the first 90 g egg whites on low.
Boil the water and castor sugar without stirring. At 114°C turn the mixer to full; the whites must be at stiff peaks when the syrup reaches 118°C. Pour in the syrup.
Mix the colouring and the second 90 g whites into the almond mix to make a black paste.

Cool 10 minutes, turn out onto a rack over a tray and pierce the tops.

100 g Dutch Boerenkaas, grated (about a cup)

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Off the heat, add the liqueur and chill a few hours.
Stir in the nougat, roll into balls and coat in vermicelli or cocoa and icing sugar.

ingredients: 320 g Sally Williams nougat, frozen and chopped
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line 1 or 2 baking sheets.
Beat the whites with the salt until frothy, add the sugar gradually and beat to stiff peaks. Fold in the cornflour.
Spoon 6 nests, building up the sides.
Turn the oven down to 160°C and bake 20 minutes, then switch off and leave 40 minutes. Cool.
Whip the cream, fill the nests, add fruit and top with nougat.

data.title: Smoked Angelfish with Lemon Marmalade & Celeriac Confit
data.headnote: Pan-smoked angelfish with a sharp lemon marmalade, celeriac confited in duck fat, apple, celery and walnut.

groups.heading: Fish
steps: Season the fish and lay it on a perforated tray covered with foil.
Put the wood chips and spices in a roasting tray of the same size (your smoker) and heat on the stove until smoking.
Set the fish tray on top and smoke over medium heat for 6 minutes. Rest 5 minutes before uncovering, then drizzle with oil.

groups.heading: Marmalade
steps: Peel the lemon rind with no white pith. Boil the sugar and water, add the rind and simmer 30 minutes until soft.
Pulse in a processor with the vinegar, castor sugar, oil and lemon juice to a marmalade.

groups.heading: Celeriac
steps: Warm the fat with the garlic and thyme in a roasting tray.
Peel the celeriac, cut discs with a pastry cutter and add to the fat with the stem pieces. Cover and cook at 90°C for an hour. Cool in the fat.
Cut the stems into 4 cm pieces and pan-fry the discs on one side until golden.

groups.heading: Plate
steps: Julienne the apple and celery and grate the toasted walnuts.
Plate the fish with celeriac and marmalade, garnish with apple, celery, walnut, dill and coriander.

data.title: Superhero Mocktails
data.headnote: Four alcohol-free drinks named after superheroes, all built by parts so you can scale them to any glass. If you use cranberry or strawberry concentrate, dilute it 1:1 with water rather than the usual 1:3 or 1:4.

groups.heading: Batkid
ingredients: Tabasco (about a dozen drops per glass)

groups.heading: Catwoman
ingredients: 1 part coffee (as strong as you like), or 2 parts cream and 2 parts coffee

groups.heading: Method
steps: Bamse: shake with ice and strain into a small glass with some ice. Serve with a blue straw; the honey sinks, so it needs stirring.
Bamse beer mocktail: build in a tankard, stirring as you add the honey. Ice is optional.
Batkid: build in a highball glass, add some ice and garnish.
Catwoman: shake without ice and serve in a cocktail glass. Grate over some lime chocolate.

data.title: Croque Monsieur Breakfast Casserole
data.headnote: Day-old croissants soaked in a mustardy custard with ham and Gruyère. A different, eggier take on the Vol. 1 croissant croque monsieur.

ingredients: 4 to 5 day-old croissants (a good handful), torn into pieces
steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Layer the croissants, ham and Gruyère in a baking dish.
In a separate bowl, whisk the remaining ingredients (except the chives) until smooth.
Pour over the croissants, top with fresh thyme and bake 30 to 40 minutes until golden and bubbly. Finish with chives.

resolvedChecks.note: "A handful" of croissants is vague; for 8 eggs and 2 cups cream, about 4 to 5 croissants fills a standard dish.
resolvedChecks.resolution: Croissants set at 4 to 5.

ingredients: 200 ml (¾ cup plus 4 tsp) warm water
15 ml (1 tbsp) olive oil, for glazing, plus extra for the tray
A handful of white and black sesame seeds
steps: Mix the flour, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Make a well, add the yeast and pour in the water. Mix with your hands; the dough should be very wet and fairly hard to handle.
Cover with cling film and prove about 1 hour, until doubled.
Tip onto a well-floured surface (use plenty of flour so it doesn't stick) and shape into a flat round about 2 to 3 cm high.
Put on an oiled baking tray, cover with a tea towel and prove another 45 minutes. Preheat the oven to 250°C for the last 20 minutes.
With your fingertips, dent a rough circle about 3 cm in from the edge, then fill the centre with criss-cross diagonal lines 2 to 3 cm apart.
Brush with olive oil, sprinkle with the sesame seeds and press them in.
Bake 8 minutes at 250°C, then turn down to 200°C and bake about 5 minutes more, until golden.

data.title: Wild Mushroom Tortellini

groups.heading: Pasta
steps: Make a well in a mound of flour, add the egg and slowly work the flour in until shaggy. Knead until it comes together, wrap and rest in the fridge.

groups.heading: Duxelles
steps: Sauté the onion, garlic and thyme until translucent. Add the mushrooms and cook until all the moisture has gone. Cool before using.

groups.heading: Shape and cook
steps: Roll the pasta as thin as possible (it swells when cooked) and cut circles with a medium cookie cutter.
Put a teaspoon of duxelles in the middle of each circle. Brush the edge with egg yolk as glue and fold into a half-moon.
Dab yolk on one corner and wrap the other corner around to meet it.
Cook in salted simmering water until al dente, about 3 minutes.

tips: Serve with brown butter and sage, or a little cream and Parmesan.

data.title: Caesar Salad the Easy Way
data.headnote: A shortcut Caesar on a mayonnaise base, blitzed in the processor.

ingredients: ½ cup good mayonnaise (Hellmann's or NOMU)
4 anchovy fillets (or up to a whole small jar)
steps: Blitz the mayonnaise, water, garlic, vinegar, Worcestershire, Tabasco and anchovies until very fine, in a food processor or with a stick blender.
Chop the lettuce into large pieces, rinse and dry, and toss with the dressing.
Grate the Parmesan over, add croutons and toss again.

data.title: Caesar Salad with Brioche Garlic Croutons

groups.heading: Dressing
steps: Chop the anchovies finely, grate the garlic just as finely and mix together.
Put the yolks in a bowl. (To avoid raw yolks, lower the whole eggs into boiling water for 1 minute, plunge into iced water, then crack the tops and spoon out the yolks.)
Beat the yolks with a balloon whisk, add the lemon juice and mustard and beat well. Gradually whisk in the oil, then the Parmesan and anchovy mix. Season with pepper.

groups.heading: Brioche garlic croutons
ingredients: Olive oil (about 1 cm deep in the pan)

groups.heading: Croutons
steps: Slice the crusts off the brioche and tear into bite-sized pieces.
Heat the oil (about 1 cm deep) and garlic in a large saucepan over moderate heat. Fry the brioche in batches until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towel.

groups.heading: Serve
steps: Halve the lettuces and arrange on a platter. Top with anchovies and croutons, pour over the dressing and serve immediately.

data.title: Restaurant Purees: Celeriac, Carrot, Courgette & Cauliflower
data.headnote: Professional-kitchen prep notes written for a Thermomix. The celeriac, courgette and cauliflower quantities are restaurant batches; halve or quarter them at home.

groups.heading: Courgette skin and herb puree
ingredients: Ricotta, to serve (500 g per 1 kg puree)

groups.heading: Celeriac
steps: Brown the butter in a large pan over high heat. Add the celeriac and cook over medium heat at least 2 hours, stirring often, until soft and the moisture has evaporated.
Toast and crush the coriander and peppercorns. Heat the milk and cream to 80°C, add the thyme and spices and infuse 1 hour. Strain.
Add half the infused milk to the celeriac and reheat gently. Blend on high (Thermomix speed 8) 3 to 5 minutes, adding the rest of the milk until silky and pipeable. Season.

groups.heading: Carrot
steps: Put the carrots, water, butter and salt in a saucepan, boil, then cover and simmer on low 20 minutes until tender.
Lift into a blender with a slotted spoon, add ½ cup cooking liquid and 1 tbsp lemon juice and blend smooth, adding liquid as needed. Season with salt and lemon.

groups.heading: Courgette
steps: Trim the courgettes, keeping only the green skin. Heat the oil, add the chopped skin and cook on high 5 to 10 minutes.
Strip the thick basil stems and chop the rest. Add the basil, chives, salt and garlic and sweat 5 minutes more.
Blend on high 3 minutes, adding up to 50 ml water if needed. Season and chill quickly over ice. To serve, mix 1 kg puree with 500 g ricotta.

groups.heading: Cauliflower
steps: Heat the butter and oil in a large pan over high heat. Add the cauliflower, cover with a cartouche and sweat 20 minutes.
Remove the cartouche and cook until deeply golden and very soft.
Add the cream, Parmesan and vinegar, simmer, then take off the heat.
Blend on high 5 minutes, adding milk for a silky, spoonable texture. Season.

data.title: Beef Wellington with Spinach Pancakes & Chicken Mousse
data.headnote: The full restaurant version: the fillet is wrapped in thin spinach crêpes and a layer of chicken-mushroom mousse before the pastry, which keeps the pastry crisp.

groups.heading: Beef
ingredients: Egg wash (1 egg beaten with 1 tbsp water)

groups.heading: Chicken mousse
ingredients: 400 g chicken breast, cubed and semi-frozen
steps: Blitz the chicken, egg and salt in a cold food processor, scraping down, to a smooth, shiny paste. Move to a bowl set over ice.
Fold in the cold cream by hand with a firm spatula (the processor would split it). Keep refrigerated, then fold in the cooled duxelles.

groups.heading: Spinach pancakes
steps: Blend the spinach, eggs, flour and milk on high about 3 minutes until smooth. Rest 30 minutes.
Wipe a hot pan with a little oil, ladle in a little batter and swirl very thin. Cook about 45 seconds a side on low-medium without colouring. Cool.

groups.heading: Duxelles
steps: Roughly chop the mushrooms in a food processor. Sweat the shallot in a little oil until translucent, add the garlic for a minute.
Add the mushrooms and cook over medium-high heat, stirring, until all the moisture evaporates. Season and cool.

groups.heading: Assemble and bake
steps: Season the beef and sear in a very hot pan until dark golden all over, 2 to 3 minutes a side. Cool.
Wrap tightly in cling film and chill at least 30 minutes. Unwrap and brush with Dijon.
Lay the spinach pancakes on a sheet of cling film, overlapping, about 2 cm wider than the beef on all sides.
Spread a 2 cm layer of the mousse-duxelles mix over the pancakes, lay the beef on top and roll up tightly in the cling film. Chill 30 minutes.
Unwrap, place on the puff pastry and roll, sealing the edges. Trim the excess and tuck in the ends. Brush with egg wash.
Preheat the oven to 220°C. Bake on a lined tray 12 minutes, then reduce to 180°C for about 22 minutes more, until the core reads about 30°C for medium-rare.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing.

data.source: Notes app (#recipe), notes from a YouTube video
checks: The note gives two core temperatures (30°C, then "38-45°C"); 30°C out of the oven rises during resting. Use a probe and check your target.

data.title: Charred Cabbage with Miso Butter
data.headnote: Budget-friendly and packed with umami. An amazing side dish, or serve simply with steamed rice and kimchi.

ingredients: 1 savoy or green cabbage, cut into wedges
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and slowly heat a cast-iron or heavy pan on the stove.
Put the cabbage wedges cut-side down in the dry pan and weigh them down (a small tray with something heavy on top). Cook a few minutes until well charred, then turn, cover and char the other side.
Mix everything for the miso butter except the water, then add hot water a spoonful at a time until it's like yoghurt.
Uncover the cabbage and pour the miso butter evenly over the top.
Cover again and bake 15 to 20 minutes until tender, uncovering for the last few minutes to colour. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

data.source: Notes app (#recipe), food blog post dated 2 October 2022

data.title: Chef's Beef Bourguignon
data.headnote: For anyone who wants to learn how chefs build flavour. Three cuts of beef, braised until falling apart, with the garnish cooked separately and added at the end.

ingredients: 750 g chuck, off the bone, cubed
250 g small button mushrooms, stems trimmed and quartered
steps: Lightly dust all the meat in the seasoned flour and tap off the excess.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat and brown the meat on all sides in batches. Set aside.

Add a bit more oil and the onion, carrots, garlic and tomato purée. Turn off the heat and put the lid on so the vegetables steam; halfway through, add the thyme, parsley stems and bay. Scrape up the brown bits, then remove the vegetables.
Add the whole bottle of wine and reduce by half.
Return the meat, vegetables and herbs and cover with the stock. Bring to a simmer, cover with a cartouche and the lid and braise in a 160°C oven for 4 to 6 hours, until very tender.
Cool the meat in the liquid. Strain, keeping the meat and discarding the vegetables and herbs.
Reduce the liquid to a coating consistency, skimming off the fat.

In a sauté pan, cook the mushrooms in a little butter until tender; set aside. In the same pan, crisp the lardons; remove and keep the fat. Cook the pearl onions in the fat with a nub of butter until tender and golden.
Return the meat and garnish to the sauce, warm through, scatter with parsley and serve with mash.

data.source: Notes app (#recipe), notes from a chef's video guide

data.title: Chilli Crisp Oil

steps: Heat the oil on high, add the onion and fry until golden. Add the fresh chilli and ginger.
Reduce the heat slightly and add the garlic, Szechuan pepper, star anise, cinnamon, cumin and dried chilli. Cook until caramelised and crispy.
Turn off the heat, then slowly add the sugar, vinegar, MSG and soy, taking care the oil doesn't boil over.
Cool slightly, then ladle into jars, about half oil and half bits. Seal and keep in the fridge.

data.title: Bertus Basson's Steamed Pork & Rice
data.headnote: A one-pot rice dish where the vegetables steam on top of the rice. Don't rinse the rice; the starch is part of the dish.

steps: Cut the pork into lardons about 1 cm wide and render in a saucepan over medium heat. Keep the rendered fat.

Bring the rice to the boil in 1 litre seasoned water (4 parts water to 1 part rice) over high heat. When the water drops just below the rice, add the green beans, baby corn, peas, lardons and the reserved fat.

data.title: Bazaar Pancakes with Cinnamon Sugar
data.headnote: Church-bazaar pancakes: thin, rolled with cinnamon sugar and served with lemon.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Sift the flour, baking powder and salt into a mixing bowl.
Beat the eggs, milk, water, lemon juice and oil together in another bowl.
Make a well in the dry ingredients, pour in the egg mixture and beat with a balloon whisk until there are no lumps. Cover with a tea towel and rest 30 minutes.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil, lower to a simmer and put a large plate over it, with a lid ready. This keeps the pancakes warm.
Mix the sugar and cinnamon.
Heat a 24 cm non-stick crêpe pan. Ladle in batter and swirl to cover the base. Cook about 1 minute, turn and cook another minute.
Put each pancake on the warm plate, sprinkle with cinnamon sugar and cover. Repeat with the rest of the batter.

data.title: Bacon & Pea Risotto Balls
data.headnote: From the canapé episode of Padkos. Make the risotto the day before; cold risotto rolls far better.

steps: Heat the stock and keep it warm.
Melt 4 tbsp butter in a heavy pan. Soften the onion, then add the garlic and bacon and fry lightly.
Add the rice with a good splash of olive oil and stir to coat.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, letting the rice absorb each ladle before adding the next.

Blitz with a pinch of salt, a splash of olive oil and 50 ml of the stock to a purée. Set aside.

groups.heading: Balls
steps: Heat the oil over medium heat in a deep pan.
Roll the cold risotto into balls. Roll in flour, dip in egg (let the excess drip off) and coat in panko.
Fry until golden and drain on paper towel. Serve with extra pea purée if you like.

data.title: Pork Ribs with Turmeric Gnocchi, Charred Corn & Smoked Cream Cheese
data.headnote: A Padkos plate with four parts: smoked fig-leaf cream cheese, turmeric gnocchi, a corn-cob and whey sauce, and glazed spare ribs.

groups.heading: Smoked cream cheese
steps: Warm the cream cheese gently with a fig leaf for 5 minutes. Remove the leaf, put the cheese in a metal bowl and refrigerate for 2 hours to set.
Smoke for 15 minutes with another fig leaf or two on the smoker. Cool and set aside.

Mix in the Parmesan, flour, turmeric, egg and salt.
Roll into 10 cm logs, dust with flour, roll tightly in clingwrap and tie both ends, squeezing out the air.
Poach the logs for 8 minutes, then plunge into iced water.
Slice, dust with flour and fry in olive oil, butter and basil until golden.

Brown in a pan with olive oil and butter, add the stock and reduce to a glaze.

steps: Rub the mielies with oil and salt and grill slowly over medium heat until charred in places. Cut off the kernels and keep the cobs.
Melt butter in a deep pan, add the cobs, basil and whey and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the cream, simmer 3 minutes more and strain.

groups.heading: To serve
steps: Add the corn kernels to the frying gnocchi, pour in the corn sauce and let it reduce.
Plate the gnocchi with the ribs, smoked cream cheese and pumpkin seeds.

data.title: Churros with Butterscotch Sauce

Mix cinnamon and castor sugar in a bowl.

data.title: Bacon Chipotle Lasagne in the Potjie
data.time: 30 min prep, 2 hr cooking, 40 min baking (plus resting)

steps: Heat a flat pot, add a splash of oil and fry the bacon slowly so the fat renders and it crisps. Drain on paper towels.
Add the onions, celery and carrots to the bacon fat and fry until soft and browned. Add the mince and fry until the liquid cooks out and it starts to sizzle and brown.
Add the butter, herbs, garlic, chillies and paprika and fry a few minutes until fragrant. Add the tomatoes, chutney, fish sauce, beer and stock and mix well.
Lower the heat to medium-low and simmer slowly with the lid open a crack for 1½ to 2 hours, stirring now and then, until reduced and silky. Take off the heat.

groups.heading: Build and bake

Top with ragu, dollops of the cream mixture and a little bacon, cheddar and mozzarella. Repeat for 4 to 5 layers.
Finish with pasta, the cream mixture, cheddar, mozzarella, Parmesan and a little smoked paprika.

Clear a circle in the coals for the pot and surround it with medium-low coals, none touching the pot. Bake with the lid on for 30 minutes, rotating to manage hot spots, then put a few coals on the lid to brown the top. (Or bake uncovered in the oven at 180°C for 40 minutes.)
Rest at least 20 minutes before serving with salsa verde.

data.title: Sweet and Spicy Snoek with Braaied Rotis
data.headnote: Snoek, caught on a hand line, all teeth and fury. One of South Africa's most sustainable fish, given a sweet and spicy twist. Pair with a Belgian tripel.

groups.heading: Snoek
ingredients: 1 large onion, thinly sliced into rounds

groups.heading: To serve
ingredients: 6 freshly made rotis (from your local Muslim or Indian takeaway)
Sliced spring onions, fresh coriander and lime wedges

groups.heading: Method
steps: Fry the onion in the oil until soft and golden. Add the garlic for a minute, then the curry powder and chilli for another minute. Add the jam, chutney and butter and stir until melted and glossy. Take off the heat.
Put the snoek skin-side down in a large flip grid. Season and baste the flesh generously. Lay the onion rings over and baste again. Close the grid snugly without squashing.
Braai flesh-side down over hot coals about 5 minutes until the marinade and onions caramelise. Flip once and cook skin-side down about 3 minutes more, until the belly bubbles.
Rest a minute, then pull the onions and flesh off the bones. Meanwhile braai the rotis until crisp.
Pile the snoek and onions on the rotis, drizzle with leftover marinade and garnish with spring onion, coriander and lime.

data.headnote: Lamb ribs reward patience with crispy fat and succulent meat; the citrus vinaigrette cuts through the richness. Pair with a West Coast IPA.

ingredients: A small handful each chopped rosemary and thyme

groups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the beer to the boil and take off the heat. Dissolve the salt, then stir in the rest of the brine ingredients.
Score the skin of the ribs in a diamond pattern. Set up a Weber for indirect cooking with a large pile of charcoal or 6 to 8 pieces of wood for a 2-hour cook.

When the coals are white, arrange the ribs bone-side down on the cool side. Baste with brine, close the lid (vent above the meat) and keep it at 180 to 190°C. Baste every 30 minutes, adding coals as needed.
At 2 hours, check that the meat is tender. Remove the ribs, spread the coals and add more if needed, then braai fat-side down slowly to crisp the fat.
Rest 10 minutes. Whisk the vinaigrette ingredients and season. Serve the ribs hot and crisp with the vinaigrette.

data.headnote: Sweet, savoury and wrapped in a coconut-biscuit crust. A big deal in America, seldom seen on our shores. Pair with an ESB or English brown ale.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Roast the pumpkin in a large tray for 45 minutes until soft. Blitz to a smooth purée and stir in the cinnamon.

Blind bake the base 8 minutes and cool completely.
Cream the butter and sugar until light. Add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla and pumpkin purée. Sift the flour, baking powder and salt and add slowly with the machine running.
Pour into the crust and bake 45 minutes. The centre stays a little jiggly but sets as it cools. Cool completely, run a knife around the edge and unmould.
Break the bacon into shards and crush the nuts. Serve each slice with ice cream, bacon shards and nut crumble.
