data.headnote: The original recipe dates from 1924. The secret is in the leaf: Cardini meant it to be eaten with your hands, so the leaves stay whole and the bread becomes croutons.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Sauce: put the anchovies, garlic and salt in a small bowl and press-and-mix with the back of a spoon to a paste. Add the yolks, lemon juice, mustard and Worcestershire and keep mixing until combined.
Switch to a whisk and whisk while adding both oils in a thin stream to a creamy sauce. Mix in the Parmesan, taste and season.
Croutons: mix the bread and oil and fry in a moderately hot pan until golden and crisp, 5 to 6 minutes. Season.
Trim the stems off the romaine and separate the leaves. Toss in a large bowl with some of the sauce.
Scatter with croutons, shave over the Parmesan with a peeler and serve the rest of the sauce on the side.

checks: Read from a photo of small magazine print; double-check amounts against the magazine.

data.title: Caesar Five Ways
data.headnote: Five spins on the classic, all using the same Caesar sauce and croutons as the Classic Caesar Salad: make one batch of each per recipe.

groups.heading: Caesar-caprese
ingredients: 6 salad tomatoes (or tomatoes of your choice)
A handful of basil, roughly torn
steps: Slice the tomatoes and arrange on a platter. Tear over the mozzarella, then the basil. Season, scatter with croutons and spoon over the sauce.

groups.heading: Caesar chicken
ingredients: A handful of parsley, finely chopped
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Loosen the skin over the breast with your fingers. Mix the butter, zest and parsley and push it under the skin.
Put the chicken breast-up in a roasting pan, pour the stock into the pan and season. Roast 50 to 60 minutes until golden and cooked. Cool to room temperature (or serve warm).
Serve with the mangetout and the sauce.

groups.heading: Grilled Caesar
steps: Bring about 3 cm water to the boil in a pan and add the vinegar. Poach the eggs 2 to 3 minutes until soft. Lift out.
Heat a griddle pan until very hot. Brush the romaine halves with oil and grill 30 seconds a side until charred.
Arrange on a platter, top with the eggs, scatter with croutons and spoon over the sauce.

groups.heading: Roast carrot and chickpea Caesar
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Toss the onion, garlic, carrots, cumin and oil in a roasting pan and season. Roast 15 to 20 minutes until tender and starting to brown.
Add the chickpeas and roast 2 minutes more. Spoon onto a platter, pour over the sauce and garnish with herbs.

groups.heading: Braaied asparagus Caesar
steps: Light a moderate fire. Blanch the asparagus in boiling water 2 minutes, drain and pack into a hinged grid.
Brush with butter, season and braai 2 to 3 minutes until marked.
Serve with croutons and sauce, and grate over the Parmesan.

checks: Read from photos of small magazine print; double-check amounts against the magazine.

data.title: Homemade Butter

steps: Beat the cream and salt in an electric mixer on medium until thick, 2 to 3 minutes.
Turn the speed up and keep beating until it separates. Pour through a sieve and drain off the buttermilk.
Put the butter in a clean bowl and work with a wooden spoon until smooth and creamy.
Shape into a block, wrap in wax paper and chill until needed.

tips: Cook with half butter and half oil if you're stir-frying; the oil stops the butter burning before the food is done.

data.title: Smoked Trout Mille-Feuille
data.headnote: Simple but striking: think trout salad on the edge of a pastry crown. Mille-feuille means layers of deliciousness.

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Lay a sheet of phyllo on the work surface and brush with butter. Top with another sheet and brush again. Repeat with all the pastry.
Put a 30 cm cake tin on the pastry and cut out a circle. Use a 15 cm cookie cutter to cut a smaller circle in the middle, leaving a ring.
Put the ring on a lined baking tray and bake 20 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool.
Meanwhile peel the celery into ribbons with a vegetable peeler and put in iced water for 2 minutes. Mix the cream cheese and horseradish.

Separate four layers of the baked pastry and put on a platter. Spread with a few spoonfuls of the cream cheese, then a quarter of the trout, some drained celery ribbons, cucumber, salad leaves and sprouts.
Top with four more layers of pastry and repeat until everything is used, ending with filling. Serve.

checks: Read from a photo of small magazine print; the "4 sprietjies" could mean spring onions rather than sprouts.

data.title: Banana Choc Chip Cookies
data.headnote: Beyond banana bread: what to do with those overripe bananas in the fruit bowl.

steps: Whisk the butter, sugar, egg and vanilla until pale and fluffy.
Fold in the flour, bicarb, cinnamon and salt.
Stir in the chocolate chips and banana.
Dollop spoonfuls onto a greased baking tray and scatter with flaked sea salt.
Bake at 175°C until golden, 10 to 13 minutes. Cool on a wire rack.

data.title: Health Rusks (with Family Edits)
data.headnote: The typed recipe carries someone's red-pen changes: less sugar, no bran, and pumpkin seeds instead of muesli. The edited version is given here, with the original in the tips.

steps: Mix all the dry ingredients.
Melt the butter and sugar together in the microwave.
Whisk the eggs and buttermilk together.
Add the butter mixture and the milk mixture to the dry ingredients and mix well.
Bake 1 hour at 180°C.

tips: The original typed recipe: 500 ml brown or yellow sugar, 750 ml bran, 250 ml sunflower seeds, 1 to 2 cups muesli or nuts (optional), and 500 g butter or margarine.
data.source: Typed family recipe with handwritten edits (photographed)
checks: The handwritten edits are hard to read; it isn't certain whether "1½ koppie" replaces the bran or the sunflower seeds. Cutting, drying and the tin size aren't on the sheet (rusks are usually cut and dried overnight at about 100°C).

data.title: Chef Matt's Carbonara
data.headnote: So good not even Chef Matt can stop eating it.

ingredients: 200 g Parmesan, plus extra to serve
200 g streaky bacon, cut into lardons (Matt uses Richard Bosman bacon)
steps: Fry the bacon and mushrooms in a large sauté pan for 2 minutes. Add the garlic, onion and thyme, turn down the heat and sauté 3 minutes more. Deglaze with the wine and take off the heat.
Whisk the yolks in a bowl, finely grate in the Parmesan and stir to combine.
Cook the spaghetti in plenty of boiling water with a glug of oil and a generous shake of salt (it should taste like the sea) until al dente.
With tongs, lift the hot pasta straight into the egg bowl and toss so the egg coats the pasta. The heat cooks the eggs; the splash of pasta water helps.
Toss through the bacon, onion, garlic and mushroom mixture and transfer to a big serving bowl.
Finish with lemon zest and Parmesan and season to taste.

data.title: French Tomato Tart

ingredients: Puff pastry, to line a flan tin
1 kg tomatoes, peeled, seeded and crushed
steps: Roll out the puff pastry and line a greased flan tin. Gently prick the base.
Mix the eggs, crème fraîche, butter, Gruyère and tomatoes. Season.
Fill the tart and bake at 180°C for about 45 minutes.

data.source: Photographed French cookbook page (title not visible)

data.title: Easy Lemon Meringue Glasses
data.headnote: The only effort is the meringue on top. You could call it a trifle that thinks it's a meringue.

ingredients: 1 vanilla pod, split and seeds scraped
1 x 280 g Madeira cake, cut into 1 cm slices
steps: Mix the mascarpone and vanilla seeds until smooth.
Divide between 6 glasses (whisky glasses show off the layers). Put two slices of cake in each and divide the lemon curd between them.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks with an electric beater. Add the sugar gradually, beating until glossy and stiff.
Spoon the meringue onto each glass and brown with a blowtorch. Serve.

tips: No blowtorch? Brown them under the oven grill.
data.source: Afrikaans menu cookbook, Menu 06 (photographed; tips signed "Herman sê")

data.title: Coconut Biscuit Ice Cream Sandwiches

ingredients: 1 litre ice cream of your choice
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Mix the coconut, butter, whites, vanilla and sugar in a large bowl.

Line a baking tray with baking paper and spray well. Set a 10 cm cookie cutter on the tray, spoon in coconut mixture and press it firmly about 5 mm thick. Lift the cutter off and repeat to make 12 rounds.
Bake 8 to 12 minutes until golden. Carefully slide the paper off the tray and cool completely.
Sandwich balls of ice cream between the biscuits. Serve.

tips: Stir 100 g finely chopped dark chocolate into the mixture for a different flavour.
data.credit: Inspired by Donna Hay (Fresh, Fast, Simple)
data.source: Afrikaans menu cookbook (photographed; tips signed "Herman sê")

data.title: Feta, Basil & Red Onion Bread
data.headnote: If there's a shortcut in the kitchen, take it. The secret is a high oven so it gets a lovely golden crust.

ingredients: 1 x 500 g packet bought bread dough
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Dust the work surface with flour and turn out the dough.
Press flat with your hands to about 1 cm thick. Spread with pesto and crumble over the feta.
Roll into a tight sausage. Spray a 30 cm ring tin and press the dough sausage into it.
Halve the onions and press into the dough. Drizzle with oil and sprinkle with salt.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool slightly, turn out and serve lukewarm.

tips: Swap the pesto for sun-dried tomatoes in oil, puréed with their oil to a coarse paste.
data.source: Afrikaans menu cookbook, "Laatmiddagkuier" menu (photographed; tips signed "Herman sê")

data.title: Peppermint Crisp Tart

groups.heading: Filling
ingredients: 4 x 80 g slabs mint crisp chocolate

groups.heading: Method
steps: Process the biscuits to fine crumbs, add the butter, mix and press into a 20 x 20 cm dish.
Soak the gelatine in the water until spongy.
Beat the caramel and cream cheese in an electric mixer until well mixed. Gradually add the cream and beat well.
Chop the chocolate very finely in a food processor (or grate it).
Dissolve the gelatine in the microwave, or over a bowl of boiling water, until melted.
Add the chocolate and gelatine to the filling and whisk well. Pour over the base and chill until set. Garnish with chocolate curls.

data.source: Photographed cookbook page, p212 (title not visible)

data.title: Snowflake Apple Pie
data.headnote: The classic recipe off the back of the flour packet, with a hot milk syrup poured over.

groups.heading: Pie
ingredients: 1 x 385 g tin sliced pie apples

groups.heading: Method
steps: Cream the butter and castor sugar. Add the egg and beat until light and fluffy.
Sift the flour and salt and fold into the butter mixture, alternating with the milk.
Turn into a greased 23 cm pie dish and arrange the apple slices on top. Mix the sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over.
Bake at 180°C for about 40 minutes.
Syrup: heat the sugar and milk and bring to the boil until the sugar melts. Off the heat, add the essence.
Pour over the pie as it comes out of the oven. Serve hot, with custard if you like.

tips: Use 3 peeled, cored and sliced fresh green apples instead of the tin.

data.title: Must-Make Salsas
data.headnote: Make plenty and serve in small bowls on crushed ice. Your guests will think you're very fancy. Lay a colourful table and drink tequila.

groups.heading: Avocado
steps: Purée everything in a food processor on high until smooth and creamy. Season.

groups.heading: Pickled radishes
steps: Bring the vinegar, peppercorns, chillies and sugar to the boil. Put the radishes in a small glass bowl and pour over the hot vinegar. Cool to room temperature.

groups.heading: Tomato and coriander
steps: Mix everything together and season well.

data.source: Afrikaans menu cookbook, "Soort van Meksikaans" menu, p183 (photographed)

data.title: Orange & Raspberry Margarita Punch
data.headnote: Hot summer days call for something with a kick. Very refreshing and it'll quench your thirst in minutes. For a virgin version, leave out the tequila.

steps: Crush the raspberries and sugar in a large bowl with a potato masher.
Put in a large punch bowl (or a big glass jar) and pour the ice over. Add the rest of the ingredients, stir and serve.

tips: Frozen raspberries work: thaw them before crushing with the sugar and add the juice from the packet too. Any berry in season works.
data.source: Afrikaans menu cookbook, "Soort van Meksikaans" menu (photographed)

data.title: One-Pot Creamy Cauliflower Soup
data.headnote: Speedy, full of goodness and endlessly comforting. Officially soup weather in Cape Town.

ingredients: 1 large head cauliflower, trimmed and roughly chopped
A generous pinch of salt and black pepper
Flash-fried mushrooms and toasted hazelnuts, to serve (optional)
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and leeks 8 to 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and sage and cook another minute.
Add the cauliflower, stock and milk and simmer 15 minutes until the cauliflower is tender.
Off the heat, cool slightly and blend smooth. Season and serve in warm bowls, topped with golden mushrooms and toasted hazelnuts if you like.

resolvedChecks.note: The leeks are listed but the method only mentions the onion; cooking them together is assumed.
resolvedChecks.resolution: Leeks cooked with the onion.

data.title: Yorkshire Pudding
data.headnote: An English savoury "pancake" that can be served many ways. The Chef's Studio's favourite: with onion gravy.

steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Pour a tablespoon of oil into each mould of a greased muffin tin and heat in the oven at least 10 minutes.
Blitz the eggs in a blender until frothy, add the milk and blitz again.
Gradually add the flour until you have a pouring-cream consistency. Season and rest 10 minutes.
When the oil is smoking hot, open the oven and pour the batter into the moulds.
Close the door and cook 10 minutes, then turn down to 180°C and cook another 15 minutes. Don't open the door until they're golden and crisp.
Remove from the oven and out of the tin.

data.source: The Chef's Studio Instagram recipe card (screenshot)

data.title: Wild Coast Seafood Potjie with Dombolo
data.time: 20 min prep, plus dombolo proving, 1 hr cooking
data.headnote: Greg's ode to the seafood buffet with white parsley sauce on everything that he grew up eating on Transkei holidays.

groups.heading: Dombolo
steps: The dombolo take a while, so start them first. Whisk the flour, sugar, yeast and salt in a large bowl. Add the water and melted butter and mix to a dough.
Knead on a clean surface for 8 minutes until soft and supple. Oil the bowl, return the dough, cover and prove until doubled.
Turn out and divide into 7 equal balls. Put a ball in each greased enamel cup.

groups.heading: Potjie
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornflour, dissolved in ⅓ cup water
500 g yellowtail, cut into large chunks
steps: Heat oil and butter in the flat pot and soften the leeks, celery, fennel, garlic, ginger and thyme.
Add the stock, lager, fish sauce and sugar and simmer. Stir in the cornflour mixture to thicken.
Add the seafood and cream, set the dombolo cups in the pot, cover and steam until the dombolo are cooked and the seafood is just done.
Finish with parsley, spring onion, lemon, celery salt and pepper.

groups.heading: To serve
ingredients: A handful of flat-leaf parsley, chopped

checks: Only the start of the method was photographed (up to dividing the dough). The potjie steps after that are assumed from the ingredient list, not from the book.

data.title: Miso Caramel Doughnuts
data.headnote: Miso became the buzzword of MasterChef Australia: fermented soybean paste with a salty, sweet character. The caramel tastes almost like salted caramel, with the miso balancing the sweetness.

groups.heading: Doughnuts
ingredients: 350 g (625 ml) cake flour, plus extra for rolling

groups.heading: Method
steps: Put the water, milk, sugar, butter, eggs, yeast and flour in an electric mixer and beat on high with the K-beater until the dough forms a ball.
Put in a clean bowl, cover with cling film and leave somewhere warm 45 to 60 minutes until doubled.
Turn out on a floured surface and press 1 cm thick. Cut 8 cm rounds and a 2 cm hole in the middle of each.
Put on a floured tray and leave somewhere warm until doubled, about 30 minutes.
While the dough rises, bring the topping ingredients to the boil in a pot and cook 3 to 5 minutes to a caramel-like sauce.
Heat the oil and fry the doughnuts 3 to 5 minutes a side until golden. Drain on paper towel.
Dip in the warm caramel and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

checks: Read from a photo of small, angled magazine print; double-check amounts.

data.title: Mojito Cake
data.headnote: This sponge will be a hit in your house. Change the flavour with the syrup you pour over it.

groups.heading: Icing
ingredients: Zest of 2 limes, plus extra to decorate
250 g cream cheese, at room temperature

groups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Put the eggs and sugar in the bowl of an electric mixer and set over a pot of boiling water. Whisk until lukewarm (test with your fingertip).
Move the bowl to the mixer and beat on high 8 to 10 minutes until thick and foamy. Meanwhile line two 18 cm loose-bottomed tins with baking paper and spray well.
Add the butter, vanilla and flour to the egg mixture and fold in gently with a spatula. Divide between the tins and bake 25 to 30 minutes until golden and cooked.
Syrup: while the cakes bake, bring the syrup ingredients to the boil. Pour over the warm cakes and cool.
Icing: beat the ingredients until light and creamy. Put one cake on a plate and spread with half the icing. Put the second cake on top, flat side up, and pipe small rosettes with the rest.
Decorate with extra mint and lime zest.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a 23 x 23 cm tin with baking paper and grease.
Combine the flour, bicarb, cornflour and salt.
Heat the butter in a pan until brown and foamy.
Whisk the sugars in a stand mixer with the whisk attachment, adding the butter on high.
Add the eggs one at a time, whisking between each, then the vanilla.
Whisk in the dry ingredients until just combined. Fold through the chocolate and strawberries.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely in the tin, about 1 hour.
Ripple cream: simmer the strawberries, lemon juice and sugar until jammy (add a dash of water to loosen). Cool and fold through the whipped cream.

data.title: Steak Tartare Sandwich on Mosbolletjie
data.headnote: Inspired by a Joe Beef (Montreal) recipe seen on Mind of a Chef with David Chang. Steak tartare between two slices of bread makes perfect sense. Mosbolletjie's sweet aniseed flavour works brilliantly with the beef.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the beef with all the other tartare ingredients by hand. Correct the seasoning and refrigerate.
Mix the anchovy into the mayonnaise and refrigerate while you make the toast.
Toast the mosbolletjie slices and make sandwiches with a smear of anchovy mayo and a thick layer of tartare.
Trim the crusts to make them pretty (the trimmings are a treat for the chef).

data.title: Another Spoonful Pudding

steps: Cream the butter and sugar. Add the beaten eggs.
Dissolve the bicarb in the milk and add with the jam.
Sift in the dry ingredients and add the egg mixture. Add the vanilla and pour into an ovenproof dish.
Bake in a moderate oven at 180°C for 45 minutes, until light brown.

checks: The method is printed as it appears; with 1 litre milk and only cornflour as the starch it bakes like a set custard. Check before making.

data.title: Chef Shanice's Lamb Curry
data.headnote: The key to a good curry: low and slow.

steps: In a big pot over medium heat, cook the onion until golden.
Add the cardamom, cinnamon and cloves, then the hot and medium curry powders.
Add the cumin, coriander, garam masala and turmeric.
When it smells fragrant and not burnt, add the meat, then the ginger and garlic.
Turn the stove to low. Add the water gradually with the potatoes, stirring continuously to mix the spices and meat together.
Simmer until the meat is tender and flavourful. Add chopped coriander before serving.
Serve with rice or roti and cucumber raita.

data.source: The Chef's Studio Instagram recipe card (screenshot)
checks: The card lists "10 x tbsp hot curry powder" and "6x tbsp medium"; that is a lot of curry powder, so taste as you go. The garlic quantity isn't given.

data.title: Savoury Crêpe Stack with Spinach, Feta & Mushrooms
data.headnote: From a TASTE piece on crêpes by food editor Abigail, who remembers church bazaar ladies flipping pancake after pancake on gas burners.

groups.heading: Filling
ingredients: 300 g spinach, finely shredded and wilted
1 small bunch spring onions, thinly sliced
½ cup smooth low-fat cottage cheese

groups.heading: Method
steps: Pour the flour onto a clean surface and make a well. Break in the eggs, then whisk in the milk, then the mustard, butter, brandy and salt.
Heat a medium non-stick pan until very hot (spray if you like). Ladle in a little batter and tilt to spread. Fry 1 minute, flip and brown the other side. Stack between sheets of greaseproof paper.
Preheat the oven to 160°C. Combine the filling ingredients.
Put a warm crêpe in a greased pie dish and layer filling on top. Repeat with the remaining crêpes and filling.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 20 minutes more. Garnish with spring onion.

tips: Wine pairing suggested: Klein Roosboom Merlot.

Other ideas from the article: apricot jam and lemon folded into triangles; two crêpes with cream and strawberries folded into a square pocket with maple syrup; mushrooms, cream, Gruyère and ham folded into quarters and baked 5 minutes at 180°C; lemon zest in the batter and lemon curd inside; tinned apple slices cooked into the batter with honey and Greek yoghurt.

data.title: Lamb Boerewors Baked in Batter with Chilli Tomato & Onion Sauce
data.headnote: A South African toad-in-the-hole for a Thursday night. Wine suggested: Spice Route Pinotage 2011.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 230°C. Blend the eggs, milk, water, flour and salt and chill while you cook the boerewors.
Grease a 25 x 18 x 2.5 cm baking pan. Cut the boerewors to fit, add a few rosemary sprigs and bake 10 minutes until it starts to colour.
Whisk the batter if needed, pour over the boerewors and bake 15 minutes more until puffed and golden.
Heat the tomato and onion with the chilli in a saucepan until warmed through. Serve with the boerewors.

data.title: Eggs Benedict Pizza
data.headnote: Wine suggested: Villiera Cru Monro Brut Méthode Cap Classique 2007.

groups.heading: Dough
ingredients: 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus 1 tbsp for brushing

groups.heading: Toppings
ingredients: 200 g lightly smoked trout, thinly sliced
steps: Bring a pan of water to the boil and add the vinegar. Swirl a whirlpool, crack in 1 egg and cook 3 to 4 minutes. Lift out and repeat.
Blanch the asparagus in salted boiling water 45 seconds and refresh in iced water. Repeat with the spinach.

Hollandaise: set a bowl over simmering water (not touching). Whisk the yolks and water until pale and thick. Whisk in the butter a piece at a time; it thins at first, then thickens to lightly whipped cream. Off the heat, whisk in the lemon, salt and pepper.
Top the base with spinach, then the eggs, asparagus and trout. Season and drizzle with hollandaise.
Grill 5 minutes until the hollandaise browns. Serve immediately.

groups.heading: Base
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Sift the salt and sugar with the flour, add the yeast and combine.
Add the olive oil to the water, add to the flour, mix and knead 10 minutes until smooth. Roll into a ball.
Press the dough with your finger: if it springs back quickly it's kneaded enough; if not, knead 5 minutes more.
Put in a greased bowl, cover with a clean cloth and leave somewhere warm 45 minutes, until doubled.
Knock down, roll out on a lightly floured surface, put on a baking tray, brush with oil and season. Bake 15 minutes.

data.title: Tomato & Bread Salad with Anchovies and Capers
data.headnote: Get as big a range of tomatoes as you can for a clash of colour. Good every day through summer, alone or with a thin tuna steak. The toasted bread keeps 4 hours and the tomatoes 6 hours in the fridge (hold back the basil); assemble just before serving.

ingredients: 6 anchovy fillets in oil, drained and finely chopped (about 20 g)
⅓ tsp flaked salt, plus extra to finish
100 g sourdough, crusts on, sliced 2 cm thick, lightly toasted and cut into 4 cm chunks
500 g ripe tomatoes, cut into 4 cm chunks
1 lemon: finely grate 1 tsp zest, then juice to get 2 tsp
5 g basil leaves, finely chopped, plus a few to serve
1 tsp Urfa chilli flakes (or ½ tsp other chilli flakes)
steps: Put the garlic, anchovies and oil in a medium saucepan with the salt over low heat. Cook gently 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the garlic and anchovies soften when mashed. Don't let it bubble or the garlic burns.
Off the heat, add the toasted bread and toss to coat. Move the bread to a large bowl, leaving the oil in the pan.
Mix the tomatoes, lemon zest and juice, capers, parsley and basil.
To serve, add the tomatoes to the bread and toss carefully. Transfer to a platter, drizzle with the remaining anchovy oil and finish with chilli flakes and flaked salt.

data.source: Photographed cookbook page, "Raw Veg" chapter p33 (very likely Yotam Ottolenghi's SIMPLE)

data.title: No-Bake Lemon Meringue Cheesecake

groups.heading: Filling
ingredients: 500 g cream cheese, at room temperature

groups.heading: Meringue
steps: Whisk the whites, cream of tartar and sugar in a heatproof bowl over simmering water until the sugar dissolves and it reaches 70°C.
Off the heat, beat on medium-high about 5 minutes until thick, glossy and cool.
Swirl over the lemon curd like clouds, scorch with a blowtorch and dust with icing sugar.

groups.heading: Cheesecake
steps: Grease and line a 22 cm loose-bottomed tin. Mix the biscuits and butter, press into the base and about 3 cm up the sides, and chill 30 minutes.
Sprinkle the gelatine over the lemon juice, leave a few minutes, then melt in the microwave to dissolve.
Beat the cream cheese, sugar and zest, then add the slightly cooled gelatine mixture. Beat in the soured cream and fold in the whipped cream.
Spoon into the crust and chill at least 2 hours to set. Spread the lemon curd carefully on top.

groups.heading: Lemon curd
steps: Mix everything in a saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly until it thickens and starts to boil gently. Strain and cool.

checks: The lemon curd lists no sugar; check the original before making it.

data.title: Raisin Rusks (Not Sweet, Slightly Salty)
data.headnote: A big-batch buttermilk-free rusk: not sweet, slightly salty. Leave the margarine out of the fridge overnight; don't melt it in the microwave.

ingredients: 500 g margarine or butter, softened overnight at room temperature
About 1.5 litres lukewarm water, added bit by bit
steps: Mix the dry ingredients and rub in the margarine.
Add the water little by little and knead well until your hands come away dry.
Leave to rise fully in the bowl you kneaded in.
Knock down, shape into balls and pack into pans. Leave to rise fully again.
Bake about 1 hour at 180°C, then dry out well.

tips: In winter, warm the flour slightly in the microwave first; the dough rises more easily.

data.title: Royal Pasta Dough
data.headnote: Italy is full of rules and old wives' tales about pasta, and they contradict each other. The key question: does it eat well with the sauce you're pairing it with?

ingredients: 400 g good-quality Tipo 00 flour, plus extra for dusting

groups.heading: Dough
steps: Pile the flour and semolina into a large bowl and make a well. Separate the eggs and put the yolks in the well (freeze the whites for meringues).
Add the oil and 4 tbsp cold water and whip with a fork until smooth, then gradually bring in the flour. When it gets hard to mix, use floured hands to form a ball.
Knead on a floured surface about 4 minutes until smooth and elastic. It shouldn't be too wet or dry; tweak with water or flour. Wrap and rest 30 minutes.

groups.heading: Rolling out
steps: Clamp a pasta machine to a clean table. Divide the dough into four, keeping it covered with a damp cloth.

Stage 1: flatten a piece by hand and run it through the thickest setting, then the next one down. Fold in half and run through the thickest setting again; repeat a few times until super-smooth and the sheet fills the machine.

Stage 2: roll the sheet down through each setting, dusting with flour, keeping light tension so there are no kinks. About 2 mm for linguine, tagliatelle and lasagne; 1 mm for filled pasta like ravioli and tortellini.

data.title: White Chocolate Cream Cheese Ganache Sponge
data.headnote: Vanilla sponge with white chocolate cream cheese ganache and fruit. The name has "only vanilla" in it, but the word doesn't fit.

groups.heading: Sponge
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease two 25 cm loose-bottomed tins, line with paper, dust with flour and shake out.
Whisk the yolks, water, vanilla and oil and add the sugar gradually. Whisk until pale yellow and thick.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks. Sift the flour, baking powder, salt and cornflour and fold into the yolk mixture, then fold in the whites.
Divide between the tins and bake 35 minutes. Cool in the tins, then on a rack.

groups.heading: Ganache
steps: Melt the white chocolate and cool.
Mix 100 ml of the cream cheese with the yolks. Beat in the melted chocolate a spoonful at a time, then the rest of the cream cheese a spoonful at a time, beating well each time.
Beat in the butter a spoonful at a time until smooth and thick. Chill until firm enough to spread.

groups.heading: Decorations
steps: Sugared fruit: brush fruit pieces with egg white and press into castor sugar.

Chocolate shards: melt chocolate in a double boiler, spread thinly on a WizBake sheet and roll it up carefully like a newspaper. Secure and chill until hard; unroll and the chocolate breaks into shards.

groups.heading: Assemble
steps: Halve both cakes to make four layers. Spread a third of the caramel on the first layer, then a layer of ganache. Repeat until all the layers are stacked.
Cover the cake with the remaining ganache and decorate with chocolate shards and sugared fruit.

data.credit: Mareli Visser, winner of the Koekedoor competition
checks: Read from a photo of small newspaper print; double-check amounts.

data.title: Sort-of Boeuf Bourguignon (with Lamb)
data.headnote: A quick oven version of the French classic, made with lamb.

ingredients: 1 x 250 g packet bacon, coarsely chopped
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Heat the oil in a medium pot until hot.
Add the garlic, onion, carrots and bacon and stir-fry 5 to 6 minutes until the onion starts to brown. Add the lamb and fry 5 minutes more.
Add the wine, rosemary, pickling onions and mushrooms. Stir in the flour and season well.
Put the pot, uncovered, in the hot oven and bake 20 to 25 minutes until it forms a thick sauce. Serve warm.

data.source: Afrikaans menu cookbook, p136 (photographed; tips signed "Herman sê")
checks: The page caption next to it reads "genoeg vir 2 persone", which doesn't match 1.5 kg of lamb; 6 is assumed. 25 minutes is also short for lamb cubes to become tender, so check them before serving.

data.title: Cauliflower Soup with Chilli Butter
data.headnote: Cauliflower is one of the cheapest vegetables and has an unfairly bad reputation. The secret is not to overcook it and to season it well. This soup is a must-make.

ingredients: 1 head (500 g) cauliflower, broken into florets
steps: Heat the butter in a medium pot. Add the onions and garlic and stir-fry 3 minutes until starting to brown.
Add the cauliflower and stir-fry 5 minutes more. Add the chilli, stock and milk and bring to the boil.
Cook 10 to 15 minutes until soft. Season and purée in a food processor until smooth. Serve warm with sambals.

tips: For extra flavour, melt 60 ml butter over medium heat until it starts to brown, add 30 ml chilli flakes, take off the heat and spoon over the soup.
data.source: Afrikaans menu cookbook, "Kortpad Indiese geure" menu, p100 (photographed)

data.title: Shortcut Thai Green Curry
data.headnote: The author once took a cooking class in Thailand where you make green curry paste from scratch: a lot of work. Supermarkets now have pastes almost as good. The secret is good ingredients with the bought paste, and always a handful of chopped coriander.

ingredients: 1 x 80 g packet green curry paste
steps: Heat the oil in a medium pot. Add the onion, garlic and chillies and stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes until starting to brown.
Add the chicken and fry 5 minutes. Add the curry paste and fry 1 minute more.
Pour in the coconut cream, season and bring to the boil. Cook over medium heat until thick and creamy and the chicken is cooked.
Stir in the mangetout and coriander. Serve warm with cumin rice.

data.source: Afrikaans menu cookbook (photographed; tips signed "Herman sê")

data.title: Brioche Bread Buns
data.time: 20 min prep, 2-3 hr proving, 30 min baking
data.headnote: Ideal for lunchboxes, sandwiches, burger buns and with soup.

ingredients: 2 packets dried fast-acting yeast (14 g total)
630 ml whole milk, slightly warm (36°C, body temperature)
1 egg, beaten, for egg wash (or flour for dusting)
steps: Line 2 large baking trays (deep ones are even better) with baking paper.
Put the yeast, sugar, milk and melted butter in a mixing bowl, then add the flour.
Mix and knead at least 15 minutes in a stand mixer or by hand. Kneading develops the gluten; this step is very important.
Oil the bowl, add the dough, cover and prove at least 1 hour, until doubled.
Punch out the air and divide into 12 even balls (weigh the dough and divide by 12). Roll into smooth balls, cupping your hand in a circular motion or pinching underneath so they're round on top.
Put 6 on each tray, cover with large clear plastic bags and prove again until doubled and puffy, 1 to 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (fan). Dust with flour or brush with egg wash.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until golden all over.

tips: Keeps 3 days airtight; freezes for 3 months (defrost 1 to 2 hours in an airtight container).

data.title: Hungarian Mushroom Soup with Fresh Dill
data.headnote: Creamy, with hints of smokiness and great umami. The perfect bowl to warm you up in winter.

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) mushrooms, sliced (white or cremini)
3 cups vegetable stock (or chicken stock or bone broth)
1 tbsp chopped fresh dill (or 2 tsp dried)
steps: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and mushrooms and cook until the mushrooms release their liquid and it evaporates, 10 to 15 minutes.
Mix in the flour and paprika and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the stock, soy sauce and milk, bring to a gentle boil, then simmer 10 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the sour cream, lemon juice, dill and parsley. Season.

data.title: Traditional Roosterkoek
data.time: 20 min prep, 1 hr rising, 20-25 min braai

groups.heading: Bread dough
ingredients: 1 kg flour, plus extra for sprinkling
500 ml (2 cups) lukewarm water, plus extra as needed

groups.heading: Method
steps: Make a braai fire with enough coals to braai on a grid about 30 cm above them.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a big bowl and make a well in the middle.
Pour the oil and water into the well and mix with a fork until the dough starts to come together, adding water bit by bit as needed.

Turn out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic. Shape into a ball, put in a lightly oiled clean bowl, cover with cling film or a cloth and leave somewhere warm 1 hour, until doubled.
Knock down and divide into 12 to 14 pieces. Roll into balls and press flatter. Sprinkle with flour.
Put on the grid and braai 20 to 25 minutes over the coals until cooked, turning often so they brown evenly.
Serve with butter, apricot jam and grated cheddar.

data.title: Roasted Tomato Cheesecake with Parmesan Crust
data.headnote: A savoury cheesecake. The post gives ingredients and steps but no quantities.

ingredients: Breadcrumbs or crushed crackers (for the crust)
steps: Toss the cherry tomatoes with olive oil, salt and pepper and roast until blistered.
Mix breadcrumbs with melted butter and Parmesan and press into a baking dish to form the crust.
Beat the cream cheese with the ricotta (or sour cream), garlic, basil and lemon zest.
Add the eggs and mix gently. Pour over the crust.
Bake until set and lightly golden.
Top with the roasted tomatoes and garnish with fresh basil.

checks: The source gives no quantities, oven temperature or baking time, and its photos look AI-generated. Test it before relying on it.

data.title: Pumpkin Fritters with Caramel-Orange Syrup
data.headnote: The pumpkin fritter's frivolous niece. As with pampoenkoekies, cook the pumpkin dry before mashing or the poffers fall apart when you fry them.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Whisk the pumpkin, salt, eggs and flour together.
Fry teaspoonfuls in hot oil until puffed and golden. Lift out with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towel and keep warm.
Bring all the syrup ingredients except the cornflour and 15 ml milk to the boil, stirring constantly. Simmer 1 to 2 minutes.
Mix the cornflour and milk, stir in and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly. Pour over the poffertjies and serve warm.

data.title: Chicken Liver Pâté
data.headnote: Chicken livers are one of those things you either love or hate; the author falls in the first group. Eat with fresh, crusty bread, sweet-sour gherkins and a piece of mature soft cheese.

steps: Heat half the butter in a pan and fry the onion and garlic slowly until soft.
Add the livers and fry until just cooked. Add the sherry and brandy and flambé. Simmer until the alcohol cooks off. Take off the heat and cool slightly.
Process the liver mixture until smooth. Add the cream in a thin stream until velvety and spreadable.
Season and spoon into a pâté dish. Melt the rest of the butter and pour carefully over the pâté. Chill until serving.

tips: Flavour the butter for the top with herbs that complement the pâté: heat fresh bay leaves in the butter to release their flavour, and lay a leaf or two on the pâté before pouring over the butter.

data.title: Peppermint Crisp Delight Cones
data.headnote: A grown-up frozen treat that mashes together a draai roomys, a King Cone and the boere tannie classic, Peppermint Crisp tart.

ingredients: 2 tins (380 g each) Nestlé Caramel Treat
8 sheets baking paper, roughly A5 size
steps: Paddle 1 tin of caramel in a bowl with a spatula until smooth. Finely grate three Peppermint Crisp bars and break the other two into chunks for garnish.
Whisk the cream and vanilla seeds until firm. Fold into the caramel, then fold in the grated Peppermint Crisp.
Wrap each cone in paper to form a collar about 5 cm above the cone and secure with tape.
Put the second tin of caramel in a piping bag and pipe some into the bottom of each cone. Fill with the Peppermint Crisp mixture so it sticks up above the cone.
Freeze standing up, preferably overnight (cut holes in an upturned ice cream container to hold them).
To serve, remove the collars and garnish with the Peppermint Crisp chunks. Good with extra whipped cream and caramel popcorn.

data.title: Koeksister Ice Cream

steps: Bring the milk, cream, half the sugar and a pinch of cinnamon to the boil. (The sugar sinks and stops the milk burning.)
Meanwhile cream the yolks and the rest of the sugar in a mixer on high. Lower the speed and add the scalding milk mixture to make a smooth custard; the heat of the milk cooks the yolks.
Cool completely, then churn in an ice cream machine until smooth.
Near the end of churning, add the koeksister pieces. Spoon into a lidded container and freeze.

tips: Cheat's version: soften bought vanilla ice cream, mix in the chopped koeksisters and refreeze. Also works with leftover Christmas pudding.
data.source: Photographed cookbook page (same book as Peppermint Crisp Delight Cones)

data.title: Sort-of Bobotie with Honey Peaches
data.headnote: The author doesn't brown the mince separately; it cooks in the oven with the custard. The peaches are a different take on blatjang.

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Heat the oil in a medium pot, add the onions and garlic and stir-fry 3 to 5 minutes until starting to brown. Add the spices and fry 1 minute more.
Put the mince in a large bowl, add the onion mixture and tomatoes, season and mix.
Spoon into an ovenproof dish about 3 cm deep and press the bay leaves into the meat.
Whisk the milk and eggs, pour over and bake 30 to 35 minutes until golden and cooked.
While the bobotie bakes, put the peaches cut side up on a baking tray, sprinkle with the sugar and bake alongside until golden.

tips: For something fresh on the side, thinly slice onions and tomatoes, drizzle with olive oil and white wine vinegar, season and sprinkle with chopped red chilli.

data.title: Handwritten Roti & Samoosa Notes
data.headnote: Quick notes from a notebook: a roti dough, a curry spice mix and a samoosa filling idea.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Roti: mix the flour, salt and water to a dough. Roll out, spread with butter, roll up into a spiral, flatten and roll out again.
Spice mix: fry finely chopped onion until brown without oil, then add the spices with a little water. Add chicken and potato, then potato sauce, and cook.
Samoosas: mix the cheese, onion and spice and fold into the pastry.

checks: These are rough handwritten notes. Cooking times and the frying method for the roti are not given.

data.title: Air-Fryer Pull-Apart Milk Rolls
data.headnote: Kids and adults love these pull-apart rolls, and they're great with a pasta dinner.

ingredients: 230 g Eureka Mills white bread flour
To activate the yeast: 3 tbsp warm water and 1 tsp sugar
Parchment paper, to line the air fryer
steps: Mix the yeast, warm water and sugar in a bowl and leave 10 minutes.
Add the flour, sugar, salt, milk and yeast mixture to a mixing bowl and knead until a rough dough forms.
Add the butter 1 tbsp at a time and knead. A sticky dough will form; don't add more flour. Knead until all the butter is absorbed, about 5 minutes.
Cover and rest somewhere warm until doubled.
Punch out the air and divide into 8 balls.
Line the bottom of the air fryer with parchment (leave the sides). Put the balls on the paper and leave until doubled again.
Preheat the air fryer to 160°C for 5 minutes, then bake 18 to 20 minutes.
Brush with butter while still warm.

tips: Cover your palms in a little olive or vegetable oil when you handle the dough to stop it sticking.

data.title: Milk Tart Croquembouche
data.headnote: A challenge from her Facebook friends: build a croquembouche with a South African twist. "Croquembouche" means "crunch in the mouth". A Moroccan tagine lid makes the perfect cone mould.

groups.heading: Choux puffs (double for a tagine lid)
Milk tart filling
ingredients: 50 g cornflour (Maizena), mixed with a little of the measured milk
3 drops almond essence (or essence of your choice)

groups.heading: Choux
steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Bring the water to the boil in a medium pot, add the butter and stir until melted.

Add the flour all at once and stir fast with a wooden spoon until it leaves the sides and forms a ball. Take off the heat and beat in the eggs one at a time, beating well after each; it must be stiff.
Line two trays with baking paper. Pipe 2 cm rounds and press the tips down with a wet finger.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, then lower to 160°C and bake 20 minutes more. Make a small hole under each with a sosatie stick and cool on a rack.

groups.heading: Filling
steps: Bring the milk, sugar and salt to the boil. Whisk the yolks into the cornflour mixture, then very slowly whisk the hot milk in.
Cook 5 minutes, stirring constantly with a whisk. Add the essence and butter and mix well.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks and fold in. Cool, then pipe into the puffs through a 1 cm nozzle.

groups.heading: Caramel and assembly
steps: Fill a big bowl with iced water. Heat the sugar and water over medium heat without stirring. Boil until golden, then dip the base of the pot in the iced water to stop it cooking.
Dip the bottom of each filled puff in caramel and stack them tightly in a cone. The caramel holds them together.

tips: Bake the puffs a day ahead and keep airtight; fill them on the day. The croquembouche can be assembled three to four hours ahead.
checks: Read from photographed newspaper print; double-check amounts.

data.title: Katkoppe (Vetkoek Meatballs)
data.headnote: Mrs Botma says they often travel long distances, and these "cat heads" are handy to eat in the car. Meatballs and vetkoek at the same time.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the bread in milk. When soaked, squeeze out as much milk as possible and crumble the bread finely; keep the milk for the batter.
Add the mince, onion, eggs, vinegar, flour, salt, baking powder, braai spice, flavour enhancer and pepper to the bread and mix. Shape into small meatballs.
Beat the flour, baking powder, eggs, salt and milk together until smooth and lump-free.
Dip the raw meatballs in the batter and fry over medium heat in hot, deep oil until light brown and cooked through. Drain on paper towel.

data.credit: Mrs Marie Botma of Koes, Namibia (then South West Africa)

steps: Whisk the eggs and yolks in a saucepan until well combined.
Add the butter, sugar, lemon juice and zest and put over medium heat.
Stir constantly until the butter melts and the curd thickens and turns glossy and smooth.
Pour into clean glass jars and cool to room temperature before closing.
Keeps up to a month in the fridge.

data.title: A Little Spanish Table: Six Tapas Classics
data.headnote: Six simple Spanish dishes from one carousel, each built around good olive oil.

groups.heading: Pa amb tomàquet (Catalan tomato bread)
ingredients: Flaky sea salt and black pepper

groups.heading: Gambas al ajillo (garlic prawns)
ingredients: 6 garlic cloves, whole or lightly smashed
⅓ cup extra virgin olive oil

groups.heading: Escalivada (Catalan roast vegetables)
ingredients: Flaky sea salt and black pepper

groups.heading: Tortilla española (potato omelette)
ingredients: ½ cup extra virgin olive oil

groups.heading: Pa amb tomàquet
steps: Grill or toast the bread until the edges are charred and crisp.
Rub the cut garlic over the hot toast. Halve the tomatoes and grate the cut side on a box grater, discarding the skin.
Spread the pulp to the edges, pour over the oil and finish with salt and pepper. Eat straight away.

groups.heading: Gambas al ajillo
steps: Warm the oil gently with the garlic (starting cold draws out the sweet flavour).
Once the garlic is pale gold and fragrant, raise the heat and add the prawns in a single layer. Cook until just pink and curled.
Off the heat, stir in the lemon and parsley. Serve straight away with bread to mop up the oil.

groups.heading: Escalivada
steps: Roast the whole vegetables at high heat until the skins blister and char all over.
Steam in a covered bowl so the skins loosen. Peel and tear into long strips.
Arrange on a plate, pour over the oil and finish with salt, herbs and pepper. Rest a few minutes before serving.

groups.heading: Potaje de garbanzos
steps: Brown the chorizo in the oil, then add the garlic and tomato and cook down.
Stir in the paprika briefly, then the stock and chickpeas and simmer until creamy.
Fold in the spinach in the last few minutes. Serve topped with the eggs and a drizzle of oil.

groups.heading: Tortilla española
steps: Cook the potatoes and onion slowly in the oil until tender, then drain, saving the oil.
Beat the eggs with salt and fold in the warm potatoes. Rest a few minutes.
Cook in a little of the reserved oil over medium heat until the edges set but the centre is soft. Flip onto a plate, slide back and finish so the middle is barely set.

data.credit: Healthy Eating Feed and Real Food Ritual (@healthyeatingfeed, @realfoodritual)
checks: The carousel had six recipes; only five were photographed clearly.

data.title: Patatas Bravas (Spicy Fried Potatoes)

ingredients: ⅓ cup extra virgin olive oil
steps: Fry the potatoes in the oil over medium heat until deeply golden and crisp. A slow fry gives the crackly shell.
Make the bravas sauce: cook the garlic, tomatoes, paprika and cayenne until thick and glossy. Season.
Pile the potatoes in a bowl and spoon the warm sauce over.
Finish with aïoli and parsley and serve while crisp.

tips: Don't crowd the pan; too many potatoes drop the oil temperature and they go soft.
data.credit: Healthy Eating Feed and Real Food Ritual (@healthyeatingfeed, @realfoodritual)

data.title: Beef Broth with Roasted Marrow Bones
data.headnote: An ultra-refined dish you'd find at some of the best restaurants, but don't be intimidated. Let the marrow slowly infuse the broth and you have an elegant starter.

groups.heading: Broth
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Roast the soup bones uncovered in a large roasting pan for 30 minutes. Add the carrots, celery and onions and roast 30 minutes more. Drain off the fat.
Move the bones and vegetables to a large saucepan. Add the 125 ml warm water to the roasting pan to loosen the browned bits and add all the pan juices to the saucepan.
Add the rest of the ingredients and enough cold water to just cover.
Bring slowly to the boil, then simmer uncovered 4 to 5 hours, topping up with water for the first 2 hours to keep everything covered. Season.
Strain through a cheesecloth-lined colander and discard the bones and vegetables.

groups.heading: Marrow bones and serving
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Roast the marrow bones on a foil-lined tray until the marrow is soft, translucent and starting to separate from the bone, about 15 minutes.
Spoon the hot broth into bowls and put two marrow bones in each. Serve immediately.

tips: Broth bank: covered, the broth keeps 3 days in the fridge or 4 to 6 months frozen.
data.source: Photographed cookbook page, "Soups and Broths" chapter

data.title: G.O.A.T. Sandwich Bread
data.time: 30 min prep, 2 hr proving, 35 min baking
data.headnote: The author's most-made bread: for butter, toast, sandwiches, breadcrumbs, croutons, fairy bread and croque monsieurs. So soft, with an amazingly golden crust and a nice chew.

ingredients: 8 g bread improver (or a pinch of vitamin C)
40 ml vegetable oil, plus extra for greasing
steps: Mix both flours, the sugar, salt, milk powder, yeast, bread improver, water and oil in a bowl to a dough.
Turn out and slap and fold: slap it down, fold it over itself with both hands, rotate 90 degrees and repeat for 5 to 6 minutes until no longer sticky (or mix on high in a stand mixer for 10 minutes).
Knead until the dough stretches thin enough to be translucent without tearing (the windowpane test). Shape into a ball, put in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and rest 1 hour, until doubled.
Punch out the air and roll out on a floured surface to 60 x 12 cm. Roll up tightly from the short end, pinch the seams shut and close the ends.
Put in a buttered loaf pan, cover with a plastic bag and prove 45 minutes, until doubled and above the pan. Preheat the oven to 180°C 15 minutes into the proof.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until golden brown. Cool completely.

data.source: Photographed cookbook page, "Bread That Will Make You Crumb" p35

data.title: Peppermint Crisp Braai Pie
data.headnote: The classic Peppermint Crisp tart taken to a whole new level, on the braai.

ingredients: 2 x 400 g rolls puff pastry, thawed
Ice cream of your choice, to serve
steps: Prepare the fire: you need medium-high coals to cook the pastry evenly without burning.
Mix the caramel in a bowl until smooth so it spreads easily. Chop or grate the chocolate finely.
Unroll a sheet of pastry onto a sprayed hinged grid, removing the plastic. Spread with caramel and sprinkle with chocolate.
Put the second sheet on top and pinch the sides closed.
Close the grid and cook over the coals 10 to 15 minutes a side until golden and cooked through.
Slide onto a board, cut and serve with ice cream.

tips: Spray the inside of the grid with non-stick spray so the pastry doesn't stick.

data.title: By the Seashore: Seared Scallops with Pak Choi & Pickles
data.headnote: A restaurant plate: seared scallops, a paper-thin dried scallop crisp, buttered pak choi, asparagus ribbons, and pickled shimeji mushrooms and radishes.

groups.heading: Seared scallops
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Remove the roe and rinse the scallops under cold water to remove sand (hold each in your palm so it doesn't break). Press dry on a clean cloth.
Melt the butter and pour into a baking tray; it should cover the scallops once they're seared.
Heat a frying pan. Dust both sides of the scallops lightly with cornflour and season with Maldon salt.
Sear until evenly golden on both sides without overcooking, then move to the buttered tray and finish in the oven until just cooked.

groups.heading: Dried scallop crisp
steps: Remove the roe and rinse under running cold water. Slice paper-thin and lay on a baking tray as close together as possible without overlapping.
Sprinkle with Maldon salt, cover with wax paper and roll with a rolling pin into a paper-thin sheet.
Dry in the oven at 70°C with the fan on for 2 to 3 hours, until dry, crisp and colourless.

groups.heading: Pak choi
steps: Melt the butter in a small pot with the water and bring to the boil.
Trim the stems and use only the leaves. Blanch in the butter water until cooked, then drain on paper towel. Season with salt if needed.

groups.heading: Asparagus ribbons
steps: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil.
Shave thin ribbons from the asparagus with a peeler, starting at the base so the tips don't break.
Blanch until tender and season with salt.

groups.heading: Pickled radishes
ingredients: 20 ml aged white balsamic vinegar (Giuseppe Giusti)

groups.heading: Pickled shimeji and radishes
steps: Shimeji: whisk the balsamic glaze, lemon oil and salt. Blanch the mushrooms and marinate in the pickle for at least 30 minutes.
Radishes: whisk the vinegar, oils and salt. Slice the radishes very thinly lengthways on a mandoline (1 to 2 mm), blanch for a few seconds and put in the pickle.

checks: The plating instructions and a final butternut component are on pages that weren't photographed clearly.

data.title: Earl Grey Granita with Lemon & Honey Ice Cream
data.headnote: Served in a small frozen teacup: a spoon of tea granita topped with lemon-honey ice cream and a candied lime slice.

groups.heading: Lemon and honey syrup
ingredients: Juice and zest of ½ lemon

groups.heading: Granita
steps: Steep the teabag in 1 litre water heated to 80°C. Stir in the sugar and bergamot and leave about 10 minutes.
Heat the glucose in a small pot until it bubbles slightly. Remove the teabag, add the glucose and cool.
Churn well in an ice cream machine, then keep in an airtight container in the freezer.

groups.heading: Syrup and ice cream
steps: Heat the honey and lemon juice, stir in the zest, take off the heat and strain.
Bring the milk and cream to the boil. Whisk the yolk and sugar, pour in the hot milk slowly and return to the heat to thicken. Add the 20 ml syrup, cool with cling film on the surface and churn.

groups.heading: Lime and serving
steps: Halve the lime and slice thinly. Bring the sugar and a splash of water to the boil, add the slices and cool. Dry in the oven at 80°C briefly until crisp.
Freeze small teacups. Put 1 tsp granita in each, pipe 30 ml ice cream on top and smooth with the back of a spoon. Finish with a lime slice.

data.source: Afrikaans fine-dining book, p45 (photographed; photo credit Restaurant Mosaic)

data.title: Party Kebabs for 50: Boerewors & Turkish Lamb
data.headnote: A catering list for a big event: boerewors kebabs with peri-peri tomato smoor in hotdog buns, and Turkish-style lamb mince kebabs with salads and yoghurt.

ingredients: Garlic, olive oil, salt and pepper

steps: Crush the biscuits and mix with the almonds, sugar, melted butter and zest. Press into a tart tin.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar, add the lemon extract and the cornflour mixed with water, then the eggs one at a time.
Pour onto the base and bake until just set.

data.title: Bosduifklip Mussel Sosaties
data.headnote: Bacon-wrapped mussels with gherkin and pineapple on a stick, straight off the coals in Namaqualand.

steps: Soak wooden sosatie sticks in water.
Halve each bacon rasher and cut the gherkins and pineapple into small pieces.
Thaw and clean the mussel meat well.
Wrap each mussel in bacon and thread onto the sticks, alternating with gherkin and pineapple.
Braai over medium coals for 15 to 20 minutes, until the bacon is crisp and cooked.

data.title: Stuffed Pork Fillet on the Coals
data.headnote: A whole pork fillet on the coals is one of David-Thys's specialities. They stuff it with whatever is in the fridge; on the show it was mustard, cream cheese and olives. Just don't overcook it.

ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
15 ml fresh thyme leaves, finely chopped
50 g pitted mixed olives, roughly chopped
Olive oil and basting sauce of your choice
steps: Butterfly the fillet open without cutting right through. Season well.
Spread the mustard over the inside. Mix the cream cheese and thyme and spread thickly over the mustard. Scatter with olives.
Fold the fillet closed, tie with kitchen string, rub with olive oil and season the outside.
Braai over medium coals until half-cooked, then baste after every turn until done to your liking.
Rest, covered, for at least 7 minutes. Slice and serve with potatoes and salad or vegetables.

tips: Other favourite fillings: kerriewors with sun-dried tomato, feta and rosemary; or ripe brie with sliced green fig preserve.

data.title: Tant Myntjie's Scones
data.headnote: A big-batch farm scone from the West Coast.

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a few baking trays.
Drizzle the melted butter over the flour and rub it in well. Mix in the baking powder, salt and sugar.
Whisk the milk and eggs and cut into the dry ingredients bit by bit with the soft butter. Don't overmix.
Turn out onto a floured surface, press flat by hand and cut out scones.
Bake about 15 minutes until golden. Serve with butter, jam and cheese.

data.title: Lena Swarts's Rooibos Roosterkoek
data.headnote: Clanwilliam is the rooibos capital of South Africa. On Erik and Melinda de Milander's farm, Oude Muur, roosterkoek queen Lena Swarts showed us how to make it with rooibos tea.

steps: Mix the flour, yeast and salt. Add enough rooibos to make a fairly stiff dough and knead well.
Cover and leave in a warm place to rise. Knock back and rise again.
Pinch off pieces, shape into balls and flatten slightly.
Braai over medium coals, turning often, until evenly toasted, light and hollow-sounding.
Serve with farm butter, jam and grated cheese.

data.title: Roerbrood (Stirred Boermeel Bread)
data.headnote: Sulene bakes with boermeel (wheat that is simply milled and not further processed) mixed with bread flour. The flavour and texture are wonderful. Replace with brown bread flour if you can't find boermeel.

ingredients: 3 x 250 ml (3 cups) white bread flour
Wheat kernels or mixed seeds, to sprinkle
steps: Grease two medium loaf tins very well (this bread sticks).
Mix the flours, salt, sugar and yeast. Mix the vinegar with the water and add.
Stir with a wooden spoon for about 5 minutes. It should be a slack mixture; add a little more water if it's stiff.
Spoon into the tins, cover with an oiled bag, wrap in a blanket and leave somewhere warm for 20 to 30 minutes until the tins are full.
Meanwhile preheat the oven to 180°C. Sprinkle with seeds and bake about 1 hour until golden and cooked through.

data.title: Namaqualand "Snails" (Garlic Steak Bites)
data.headnote: Not snails at all: cubes of aged rump in garlic butter, served in snail dishes under melted cheddar.

steps: Season the steak. Melt the butter and fry the garlic over low heat until fragrant. Add the lemon juice.
Fry the steak in the garlic butter until half-cooked. Rest a few minutes, then cut into 1.5 cm cubes.
Toss the cubes in the garlic butter for a few seconds.
Spoon into snail dishes (or onto spoons), spoon over garlic butter and sprinkle with cheese.
Flash under a very hot grill until the cheese melts. Serve with brown bread fingers.

data.title: Gerda Coetzee's Malva Pudding
data.headnote: A proper farm malva, from Groot Riet.

groups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a medium ovenproof dish.
Cream the butter and sugar well. Beat in the egg and milk.
Sift over the flour and ginger, add the vinegar and stir.
Mix the bicarb into the jam and add. Mix to a smooth batter and pour into the dish.
Bake about 35 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile heat the syrup ingredients over low heat until the sugar dissolves, then simmer 3 minutes.
Prick the hot pudding with a fork and spoon over the boiling syrup. Serve warm with custard.

data.source: Plaaskombuis recipes for VIA (Episode 7); Gerda's own notes

data.title: Stewed Dried Peaches
data.headnote: A Namaqualand side for venison, curries and roasts.

steps: Cover the peaches with boiling water and leave 30 minutes to plump.
Put the peaches and soaking water in a pot with the cinnamon, bring to the boil and simmer gently until soft.
Mix the custard powder and sugar with a little cold water.
Stir half into the peaches and boil for a few minutes until slightly thickened. Add the rest if you want it thicker.
Remove the cinnamon and serve.

data.title: Curried Lamb Pot
data.headnote: Served on the show with the Stewed Dried Peaches.

ingredients: 1.5 kg mutton or lamb, in pieces
steps: Brown the onions in hot oil in a heavy pot. Add the meat and jam.
Add the boiling water, cover and stew 1½ to 2 hours until tender. Add the vegetables.
30 minutes before serving, mix the curry, flour, sugar, coriander, salt, pepper and lemon juice and stir into the pot.
Serve with rice, blatjang and banana.

data.title: Lemon Meringue Tart
data.headnote: The condensed-milk classic.

groups.heading: Crust
ingredients: 1 packet (200 g) Marie or Tennis biscuits, crushed

groups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Mix the crumbs and butter and press into a small tart dish. Chill.
Whisk the condensed milk, lemon juice and yolks and pour into the crust.
Whisk the whites to stiff peaks, then add the sugar a spoon at a time until thick and glossy.
Spread the meringue over the filling, covering it completely.
Bake 15 to 25 minutes until golden. Cool to room temperature.

data.title: Shank Pie with Batter Topping
data.headnote: Pressure-cooked shank under a pour-over batter crust.

groups.heading: Filling
ingredients: 2 tbsp thick white onion soup powder

groups.heading: Method
steps: Brown the onion and meat with salt and pepper. Pressure-cook for 2 hours or until tender. Cool.
Remove the bones and shred the meat. Add the vegetables and cook through, then thicken with the soup powder.
Spoon into a greased ovenproof dish.
Whisk the egg, oil and milk. Mix the flour and salt, whisk in the wet mix until smooth, then the baking powder. Add milk if stiff.
Pour over the meat, decorate with onion rings and bake at 180°C for 20 to 30 minutes.

data.title: Molshope (Cheesy Potato Mounds)
data.headnote: "Molehills": scoops of creamy mash baked under cheese and cream.

steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water until soft. Drain, mash well and stir in the butter, cream cheese, baking powder and salt. Cool slightly.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a medium dish.
Use an ice-cream scoop to make mounds in the dish (dip the scoop in iced water if it sticks).
Sprinkle with cheese, drizzle with cream and bake 20 to 30 minutes until golden.

data.title: Sweet Potatoes with Muscadel
data.headnote: Layered, buttery, caramelised and boozy. Adapted and halved from the original.

steps: Peel the sweet potatoes, keeping them in lemon water, then cut into rough chunks.
Layer in a heavy pot with sugar and dots of butter, repeating until everything is used.
Pour over the muscadel and bring to the boil, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer about 1½ hours until soft.
Uncover and simmer until the liquid has almost cooked away and the sweet potatoes are caramelised.

data.title: Oxtail & Stampkoring Potjie
data.headnote: Oxtail braised in white wine, then finished with potatoes, mushrooms and stampkoring (cracked wheat) in the same pot.

steps: Heat the oil in a large potjie over hot coals and fry the onions for a few minutes.
Season the oxtail and brown with the onions.
Add 1 litre of wine (more if the meat isn't covered). Cover and simmer over medium coals until almost falling off the bone, up to 3 hours. Top up with wine or water as needed.
Add the potatoes and mushrooms, season, cover and simmer until the potatoes are soft.
Add a little water if needed, spread the stampkoring in an even layer and pour the braai sauce over everything.
Cover and simmer until the wheat is swollen and cooked.
Sprinkle with cheese, cover until melted, and serve.

data.credit: Jan Ponk & Renske van Zyl, Vredendal (Plaaskombuis)

data.title: Seafood Potjie
data.headnote: A West Coast paella in a flat potjie, finished with cream, cheese and parsley.

ingredients: 30 ml each sea salt and black pepper
1 to 2 raw crayfish tails, in pieces (optional)
steps: Heat the oil and butter in a large flat potjie and soften the onions, peppers and garlic.
Add the rice and fry until every grain is coated. Add the mushrooms and cook.
Add the tomatoes and half the salt and pepper. Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the seafood mix, mussel meat, calamari and the rest of the seasoning. Add the wine and cook over high heat until the rice and seafood are just done and most liquid is absorbed.
Pack the half-shell mussels on top, cover and steam about 10 minutes.
Add the cream and cook through. Add the crayfish (if using), then the parsley and cheese. Serve with lemon.

data.title: Apple Tarte Tatin with Spiced Ice Cream & Sugar Nest

groups.heading: Rough puff
steps: Mix the flour, salt and sugar with a paddle, add the butter for 1 to 2 minutes, then stream in the water until a dough forms. Flatten and freeze 20 minutes.
Cut into 4, roll each to 2 mm and cut 12 cm circles. Freeze on baking paper until firm.

groups.heading: Sugar nests
steps: Freeze two ladles. Cook the sugar and water to golden caramel, shock the pan in iced water and let it thicken slightly.
Spray the ladle bases and drizzle thin strands of caramel back and forth to make a nest. Harden, remove and repeat to make 8 nests.

groups.heading: Tarte tatin
steps: Preheat the oven to 240°C (fan). Peel the apples, top and tail, halve crossways and core.
Line 4 x 9 cm tart tins. Cook the sugar to a light caramel, add the salt and divide among the tins. Set 5 minutes.
Put an apple half on each, brush one side of the pastry with egg white and press it glazed side down over the apple, sealing the edges.
Bake 25 minutes until deep golden. Rest 2 minutes.
Invert onto plates, top with a nest, a scoop of ice cream and a second nest. Dust with icing sugar.

groups.heading: Ice cream
steps: Pre-chill the ice cream machine. Simmer the milk, cream, peel, cinnamon and salt, then infuse 15 minutes off the heat.
Whisk the yolks and sugar until light. Bring the cream back to a simmer and whisk it into the yolks. Strain into a clean pan.
Stir over medium heat until it coats a spoon, then churn and freeze.

data.title: Fish Agnolotti with Sour Fish Broth & Chilli Oil

groups.heading: Fish broth
ingredients: 4 pickled peppers, plus 1 tbsp pickling liquid

groups.heading: Stock and filling
steps: Pressure-cook the trotter, chicken feet, ginger and water on high for 20 minutes. Strain.
Fillet the fish (keep the bones). Blend about 400 g flesh with the ginger, coriander, egg whites, 10 g cornflour, pepper, sesame oil, salt, sugar, rapeseed oil and ice to a smooth paste.

groups.heading: Dough and shaping
steps: Mix 100 g of the paste with the flour and remaining cornflour, knead 5 to 7 minutes until smooth and rest 15 minutes.
Pulse the water chestnuts into the rest of the paste and pipe into a bag with a 1 cm nozzle.
Roll half the dough through a pasta machine to the second-thinnest setting. Pipe a line of filling down each sheet, fold over and seal.
Pinch at 15 to 20 mm intervals, cut the strip free and separate the agnolotti. Dust with flour and dry 15 minutes. Repeat.

groups.heading: Broth and chilli oil
steps: Sear the fish bones with half the sliced ginger in 1 tbsp oil until deep golden. Add 2 cups meat stock and boil 15 minutes to 1½ cups. Strain.
Finely chop the pickled peppers, greens, garlic and remaining ginger. Fry in 1 tbsp oil until golden, set half aside, then deglaze with the broth and pickling liquid and simmer 5 minutes.
Chop the chillies and cook gently with the oil and shrimp for 10 to 12 minutes until deep orange. Strain and keep the crisp shrimp.

groups.heading: Serve
steps: Boil the agnolotti about 3 minutes until they float. Divide among bowls, top with pickle mix, shrimp and chives, and pour over the broth and chilli oil.

data.title: Spice-Rubbed Pork with Smoked Beetroot & Hasselback Potatoes

groups.heading: Smoked beetroot purée
ingredients: 1 tsp fine wood chips (for a smoking gun)

groups.heading: Pork
steps: Toast the seeds and peppercorns 2 minutes, grind fine and add the salt.
Trim the fillet, rub with the spice and oil and chargrill 15 to 16 minutes, turning, until medium. Rest.
Whisk the dressing and season.

groups.heading: Beetroot
steps: Pressure-cook the beetroot with the orange juice and salt for 30 minutes. Peel and blend smooth with the butter, adding cooking liquid if needed. Warm 5 minutes and season.
Cover with clingwrap, fill with smoke from a smoking gun and leave 10 minutes.
Boil the pickling ingredients. Punch a 7 cm tube from the raw beetroot, slice paper-thin, pour over the hot pickle and cool.

groups.heading: Cabbage and potatoes
steps: Soften the diced shallot in butter, add crushed caraway and sliced cabbage for 2 minutes, then the wine until almost gone, then the cream for 5 minutes. Season.
Slice the potatoes every 2 mm between two chopsticks. Cook in simmering clarified butter about 25 minutes, adding the garlic after 10 and the herbs for the last 5. Drain and salt.

groups.heading: Plate
steps: Mould creamed cabbage with a 7 cm ring, add a potato and a swoosh of purée.
Slice the pork into 3 medallions, add pickled beetroot like petals, watercress and a drizzle of dressing.

data.source: MasterChef Australia recipe (Network Ten, saved PDF)

data.title: Hokkaido Scallop Crudo with Nectarine & Thai Basil

groups.heading: Garnish
ingredients: Thai basil flowers and young leaves

groups.heading: Method
steps: Halve the scallops widthways and chill. Slice the nectarines 1 mm thick on a mandoline.
Peel the ginger and lemon. Steep the ginger peel in the vinegar at a simmer for 5 minutes and strain 2 tbsp.
Juice the lemon (2½ tbsp) and ginger (2 tbsp). Blend with the vinegar, fish sauce, sugar, mirin, oils and salt and sieve into a squeeze bottle.
Blend the oil, lemon myrtle, basil and salt on high 3 minutes and strain over an ice bath.
Plate 4 nectarine slices, 5 scallop halves, dressing to cover the plate, drops of the green oil, roe and basil.

data.source: MasterChef Australia recipe (Network Ten, saved PDF)

data.title: Watermelon & Tuna Salad with Crispy Nori Chips

groups.heading: Avocado wasabi cream
ingredients: 1 spring onion and black sesame seeds, to garnish

groups.heading: Method
steps: Cut the tuna into 1.2 cm cubes, dress with sesame oil and salt and chill.
Cube the watermelon and marinate 15 minutes in the ponzu, yuzu and a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil to 180°C. Dip a rice paper sheet in water, press onto a nori sheet, pat dry and fry nori-side down 30 seconds. Drain and season with sugar and salt.
Blitz the avocado, lime juice and wasabi, season and pipe.
Drain the watermelon (keep the juice), toss with the tuna and spring onion and dome on a plate. Pipe avocado dots, sprinkle sesame and dress with the juices. Serve with nori chips.

data.title: Honey Garlic Pork Chops

ingredients: 4 pork chops, bone in or out
2 tbsp rice wine vinegar (or any white vinegar)
steps: Heat the grill. Season the chops with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Sear in the hot oil 4 to 5 minutes a side until golden and cooked. Set aside.
Lower the heat, melt the butter and scrape up the bits. Fry the garlic 30 seconds, then add the honey, water and vinegar.
Reduce on medium-high 3 to 4 minutes until slightly thick.
Return the pork, baste and grill 1 to 2 minutes until the edges char. Garnish with parsley.

tips: To bake instead, sear 2 minutes a side, baste and bake at 200°C for 10 to 15 minutes, then grill 2 minutes.

ingredients: 2 kg whole beef brisket, bone in
steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Brown the seasoned brisket in a little oil in a heavy ovenproof pot.
Rub with the spice, return to the pot and add water to a quarter of the way up.
Cover and bake 2½ to 3 hours, checking the water every 30 minutes, until the bone pulls out cleanly.
Shred the beef. Reduce the cooking liquid and strain it into the beef. Adjust the seasoning.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Roll a line of beef in each tortilla and pack seam-down in a dish.
Spread with enchilada sauce, top with the cheeses and bake 20 to 25 minutes. Garnish with coriander.

data.title: Matt Manning's Wild Boar Scotch Eggs
data.headnote: A regular at Matt's Private Kitchen Brunch Club.

ingredients: 25 g Dijon mustard, plus extra to serve
Pinch each of sea salt and black pepper

groups.heading: Method
steps: Boil the eggs 5 minutes, refresh in iced water 20 minutes and peel.
Mix the sausage meat with the mustards, herbs, yolk, breadcrumbs and seasoning. Divide into 6 and flatten each into a 1 cm patty.
Mould each patty around an egg without overlapping too much. Chill 1 hour.
Roll in salted flour, then egg, then panko, shaping in your hands. Chill 30 minutes.
Deep-fry at 180°C about 2 minutes until golden. Drain, halve lengthways and serve with Dijon.

data.title: French Onion Soup (Big Batch)
data.headnote: The success of this soup depends on your stock. Boost it with a little beef bouillon if it's weak.

ingredients: 6 large red or yellow onions (about 1.4 kg)
2 litres beef or chicken stock (or a mix)
½ cup dry vermouth or white wine
1 tbsp fresh thyme (or ½ tsp dried)
steps: Slice the onions thinly from root to stem (about 10 cups).
Cook in 3 tbsp oil over medium heat, stirring often, until soft (15 to 20 minutes).
Turn up to medium-high, add the rest of the oil and the butter and cook until browning (20 to 40 minutes).
Add the sugar and 1 tsp salt and cook 10 to 15 minutes more until well browned. Add the garlic for a minute.
Deglaze with the vermouth, then add the stock, bay and thyme. Simmer, covered, about 30 minutes.
Season, remove the bay and add the brandy.
Brush the bread with olive oil and toast at 230°C for 5 to 7 minutes. Turn, top with Gruyère and Parmesan and bake until bubbling.
Ladle the soup into bowls and float a cheesy toast on each.
